question:

 the results for analytics and visualization. How should you configure the pipeline?

option_c: 1 = BigQuery, 2 = AutoML, 3 = Cloud Functions
option_d: 1 = BigQuery, 2 = AI Platform, 3 = Cloud Storage

question:
Your organization wants to make its internal shuttle service route more efficient. The shuttles currently stop at all pick-up points across the city
 every 30 minutes between 7 am and 10 am. The development team has already built an application on Google Kubernetes Engine that requires
 users to confirm their presence and shuttle station one day in advance. What approach should you take?
option_a:
1. Build a tree-based regression model that predicts how many passengers will be picked up at each shuttle station. 2. Dispatch an
 appropriately sized shuttle and provide the map with the required stops based on the prediction.
option_b:
1. Build a tree-based classification model that predicts whether the shuttle should pick up passengers at each shuttle station. 2. Dispatch
 an available shuttle and provide the map with the required stops based on the prediction.
option_c:
1. Build a reinforcement learning model with tree-based classification models that predict the presence of passengers at shuttle stops as
 agents and a reward function around a distance-based metric. 2. Dispatch an appropriately sized shuttle and provide the map with the
 required stops based on the simulated outcome.
option_d:
1. Define the optimal route as the shortest route that passes by all shuttle stations with confirmed attendance at the given time under
 capacity constraints. 2. Dispatch an appropriately sized shuttle and indicate the required stops on the map.
explanation: The users confirm attendance and pickup location in advance, so passenger presence does not need to be predicted. This is a constrained route-optimization problem: select the shortest feasible route through the confirmed stops and choose a vehicle with sufficient capacity. No machine learning model is required.
exam_objectives: Building models given the task considering cost, complexity, latency, and scalability
topics: Agents; GKE; Classification; Regression

question:
You were asked to investigate failures of a production line component based on sensor readings. After receiving the dataset, you discover that
 less than 1% of the readings are positive examples representing failure incidents. You have tried to train several classification models, but none of
 them converge. How should you resolve the class imbalance problem?
option_a: Use the class distribution to generate 10% positive examples.
option_b: Use a convolutional neural network with max pooling and softmax activation.
option_c: Downsample the data with upweighting to create a sample with 10% positive examples.
option_d: Remove negative examples until the numbers of positive and negative examples are equal.
explanation: Verified: C. For a severely imbalanced dataset that fails to converge, Google recommends downsampling the majority class and applying upweighting so the sampled distribution trains efficiently while preserving the original class prior in the loss. A 1:1 deletion strategy can discard too much useful majority-class data.

exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: Data Preparation; Classification

question:

 your pipelines are taking over 12 hours to run. To speed up development and pipeline run time, you want to use a serverless tool and SQL syntax.
 You have already moved your raw data into Cloud Storage. How should you build the pipeline on Google Cloud while meeting the speed and
 processing requirements?
option_a: Use Data Fusion's GUI to build the transformation pipelines, and then write the data into BigQuery.
option_b: Convert your PySpark into SparkSQL queries to transform the data, and then run your pipeline on Dataproc to write the data into BigQuery.
option_c:
Ingest your data into Cloud SQL, convert your PySpark commands into SQL queries to transform the data, and then use federated queries
 from BigQuery for machine learning.
option_d:
Ingest your data into BigQuery using BigQuery Load, convert your PySpark commands into BigQuery SQL queries to transform the data, and
 then write the transformations to a new table.
explanation: Verified: D. BigQuery is serverless and supports SQL transformations with no cluster management. Data can be loaded from Cloud Storage and transformed with BigQuery SQL into new tables, matching both the serverless and SQL requirements.

question:
You work for an online retail company that is creating a visual search engine. You have set up an end-to-end ML pipeline on Google Cloud to
 classify whether an image contains your company's product. Expecting the release of new products in the near future, you configured a retraining
 functionality in the pipeline so that new data can be fed into your ML models. You also want to use AI Platform's continuous evaluation service to
 ensure that the models have high accuracy on your test dataset. What should you do?
option_a: Extend your test dataset with images of the newer products when they are introduced to retraining.
option_b: Keep the original test dataset unchanged even if newer products are incorporated into retraining.
option_c: Replace your test dataset with images of the newer products when they are introduced to retraining.
option_d: Update your test dataset with images of the newer products when your evaluation metrics drop below a pre-decided threshold.
explanation: Verified with terminology caveat: B. The evaluation set should evolve to represent both existing and newly introduced product classes; replacing it would lose regression coverage for older products, while waiting for a metric drop is reactive. “AI Platform continuous evaluation” is legacy terminology; current Vertex AI evaluation workflows use a representative ground-truth test dataset and new production data.

question:
You are developing ML models with AI Platform for image segmentation on CT scans. You frequently update your model architectures based on
 the newest available research papers, and have to rerun training on the same dataset to benchmark their performance. You want to minimize
 computation costs and manual intervention while having version control for your code. What should you do?
option_a: Use Cloud Functions to identify changes to your code in Cloud Storage and trigger a retraining job.
option_b: Use the gcloud command-line tool to submit training jobs on AI Platform when you update your code.
option_c: Use Cloud Build linked with Cloud Source Repositories to trigger retraining when new code is pushed to the repository.
option_d: Create an automated workflow in Cloud Composer that runs daily and looks for changes in code in Cloud Storage using a sensor.
explanation: Verified: C. Source-controlled code plus a Cloud Build repository trigger provides version control and automatically starts a build or training workflow on a push. Manual gcloud submission and daily polling introduce unnecessary intervention and compute delay.

question:
Your team needs to build a model that predicts whether images contain a driver's license, passport, or credit card. The data engineering team
 already built the pipeline and generated a dataset composed of 10,000 images with driver's licenses, 1,000 images with passports, and 1,000
 images with credit cards. You now have to train a model with the following label map: [`˜drivers_license', `˜passport', `˜credit_card']. Which loss
 function should you use?
option_a: Categorical hinge
option_b: Binary cross-entropy
option_c: Categorical cross-entropy
option_d: Sparse categorical cross-entropy
explanation: Verified with ambiguity noted: D is correct when the label map is used to encode each example as a single integer class ID, which is the usual meaning of a label map. Sparse categorical cross-entropy is for mutually exclusive multiclass targets represented as integers; categorical cross-entropy would be correct only if the labels had already been one-hot encoded. The question does not explicitly state the target encoding, so this assumption should be kept in mind.

question:
You have trained a deep neural network model on Google Cloud. The model has low loss on the training data, but is performing worse on the
 validation data. You want the model to be resilient to overfitting. Which strategy should you use when retraining the model?
option_a: Apply a dropout parameter of 0.2, and decrease the learning rate by a factor of 10.
option_b: Apply a L2 regularization parameter of 0.4, and decrease the learning rate by a factor of 10.
option_c: Run a hyperparameter tuning job on AI Platform to optimize for the L2 regularization and dropout parameters.
option_d: Run a hyperparameter tuning job on AI Platform to optimize for the learning rate, and increase the number of neurons by a factor of 2.
explanation: Verified: C. The gap between low training loss and worse validation performance indicates overfitting. Both dropout and L2 regularization are appropriate controls, but their optimal strengths are data- and model-dependent. A hyperparameter tuning job over both is therefore better than choosing arbitrary fixed values or increasing model capacity.
exam_objectives: Training models
topics: Model Optimization; Hyperparameter Tuning; Custom Training

question:
You built and manage a production system that is responsible for predicting sales numbers. Model accuracy is crucial, because the production
 model is required to keep up with market changes. Since being deployed to production, the model hasn't changed; however the accuracy of the
 model has steadily deteriorated.
 What issue is most likely causing the steady decline in model accuracy?
option_a: Poor data quality
option_b: Lack of model retraining
option_c: Too few layers in the model for capturing information
option_d: Incorrect data split ratio during model training, evaluation, validation, and test
explanation: Verified: B. A production model that remains unchanged while market behavior evolves becomes stale. Changes in the serving-data distribution can steadily degrade accuracy, so monitoring and retraining with newer representative data are required.

question:
You have been asked to develop an input pipeline for an ML training model that processes images from disparate sources at a low latency. You
 discover that your input data does not fit in memory. How should you create a dataset following Google-recommended best practices?
option_a: Create a tf.data.Dataset.prefetch transformation.
option_b: Convert the images to tf.Tensor objects, and then run Dataset.from_tensor_slices().
option_c: Convert the images to tf.Tensor objects, and then run tf.data.Dataset.from_tensors().
option_d: Convert the images into TFRecords, store the images in Cloud Storage, and then use the tf.data API to read the images for training.
explanation: Verified: D. The tf.data API streams file-backed datasets so the full dataset does not need to fit in memory. TFRecord is a standard efficient record format for large TensorFlow training datasets, and storing sharded TFRecords in Cloud Storage supports scalable input pipelines. Prefetch is also recommended for performance, but by itself it does not define a suitable out-of-memory dataset source.

question:
You are building a real-time prediction engine that streams files which may contain Personally Identifiable Information (PII) to Google Cloud. You
 want to use the
 Cloud Data Loss Prevention (DLP) API to scan the files. How should you ensure that the PII is not accessible by unauthorized individuals?
option_a: Stream all files to Google Cloud, and then write the data to BigQuery. Periodically conduct a bulk scan of the table using the DLP API.
option_b:
Stream all files to Google Cloud, and write batches of the data to BigQuery. While the data is being written to BigQuery, conduct a bulk scan
 of the data using the DLP API.
option_c:
Create two buckets of data: Sensitive and Non-sensitive. Write all data to the Non-sensitive bucket. Periodically conduct a bulk scan of that
 bucket using the DLP API, and move the sensitive data to the Sensitive bucket.
option_d:
Create three buckets of data: Quarantine, Sensitive, and Non-sensitive. Write all data to the Quarantine bucket. Periodically conduct a bulk
 scan of that bucket using the DLP API, and move the data to either the Sensitive or Non-Sensitive bucket.
explanation: Verified: D. Incoming files should first land in a restricted quarantine bucket so unclassified PII is never exposed through a general-access destination. Sensitive Data Protection can inspect each file and then route it to a sensitive or non-sensitive bucket according to the result.
exam_objectives: Identifying risks to AI solutions; Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: Data Privacy; BigQuery; Responsible AI

question:
You work for a large hotel chain and have been asked to assist the marketing team in gathering predictions for a targeted marketing strategy. You
 need to make predictions about user lifetime value (LTV) over the next 20 days so that marketing can be adjusted accordingly. The customer
 dataset is in BigQuery, and you are preparing the tabular data for training with AutoML Tables. This data has a time signal that is spread across
 multiple columns. How should you ensure that
 AutoML fits the best model to your data?
option_a:
Manually combine all columns that contain a time signal into an array. AIlow AutoML to interpret this array appropriately. Choose an
 automatic data split across the training, validation, and testing sets.
option_b:
Submit the data for training without performing any manual transformations. AIlow AutoML to handle the appropriate transformations.
 Choose an automatic data split across the training, validation, and testing sets.
option_c:
Submit the data for training without performing any manual transformations, and indicate an appropriate column as the Time column. AIlow
 AutoML to split your data based on the time signal provided, and reserve the more recent data for the validation and testing sets.
option_d:
Submit the data for training without performing any manual transformations. Use the columns that have a time signal to manually split your
 data. Ensure that the data in your validation set is from 30 days after the data in your training set and that the data in your testing sets from 30
 days after your validation set.
explanation: Verified: D. Because the time signal is spread across multiple columns rather than a single usable timestamp column, Google guidance recommends a manual chronological split, with earlier observations used for training and the most recent observations reserved for validation and testing. The exact 30-day spacing in the option is scenario-specific, but D is the only choice that preserves temporal ordering without inventing a combined array feature.

question:
You are an ML engineer at a regulated insurance company. You are asked to develop an insurance approval model that accepts or rejects
 insurance applications from potential customers. What factors should you consider before building the model?
option_a: Redaction, reproducibility, and explainability
option_b: Traceability, reproducibility, and explainability
option_c: Federated learning, reproducibility, and explainability
option_d: Differential privacy, federated learning, and explainability
explanation: For a regulated decision system, you need traceability for accountability and auditability, reproducibility so decisions and model versions can be recreated, and explainability so approval or rejection outcomes can be understood. Redaction and privacy techniques may also be required, but B is the only option containing the three core governance properties.
exam_objectives: Identifying risks to AI solutions; Building models given the task considering cost, complexity, latency, and scalability
topics: Responsible AI; Explainability; Data Privacy; ML Metadata

question:
You are training a Resnet model on AI Platform using TPUs to visually categorize types of defects in automobile engines. You capture the training
 profile using the
 Cloud TPU profiler plugin and observe that it is highly input-bound. You want to reduce the bottleneck and speed up your model training process.
 Which modifications should you make to the tf.data dataset? (Choose two.)
option_a: Use the interleave option for reading data.
option_b: Reduce the value of the repeat parameter.
option_c: Increase the buffer size for the shuttle option.
option_d: Set the prefetch option equal to the training batch size.
option_e: Decrease the batch size argument in your transformation.
explanation: For an input-bound tf.data pipeline, parallelizing file reads with interleave and overlapping preprocessing with model execution using prefetch are standard optimizations. Current TensorFlow guidance generally recommends tf.data.AUTOTUNE rather than setting prefetch exactly to the batch size, but A and D are the best choices provided.
exam_objectives: Choosing appropriate hardware for training; Training models
topics: Training Hardware; Pipelines; Model Optimization; Custom Training

question:
You have trained a model on a dataset that required computationally expensive preprocessing operations. You need to execute the same
 preprocessing at prediction time. You deployed the model on AI Platform for high-throughput online prediction. Which architecture should you
 use?
option_a:
Validate the accuracy of the model that you trained on preprocessed data. Create a new model that uses the raw data and is available in
 real time. Deploy the new model onto AI Platform for online prediction.
option_b:
Send incoming prediction requests to a Pub/Sub topic. Transform the incoming data using a Dataflow job. Submit a prediction request to AI
 Platform using the transformed data. Write the predictions to an outbound Pub/Sub queue.
option_c:
Stream incoming prediction request data into Cloud Spanner. Create a view to abstract your preprocessing logic. Query the view every
 second for new records. Submit a prediction request to AI Platform using the transformed data. Write the predictions to an outbound Pub/Sub
 queue.
option_d:
Send incoming prediction requests to a Pub/Sub topic. Set up a Cloud Function that is triggered when messages are published to the
 Pub/Sub topic. Implement your preprocessing logic in the Cloud Function. Submit a prediction request to AI Platform using the transformed
 data. Write the predictions to an outbound Pub/Sub queue.
explanation: Among the listed architectures, Pub/Sub plus Dataflow is the scalable choice for computationally expensive preprocessing and high throughput. Dataflow can transform requests in parallel before submitting them for prediction and publishing results. Caveat: this is an asynchronous architecture, so it does not provide low-latency synchronous online prediction; ideally, identical preprocessing would be packaged with the model or served in a low-latency preprocessing service.
exam_objectives: Serving models; Developing end-to-end ML pipelines
topics: Dataflow; Online Inference; Cloud Run; Autoscaling

question:
Your team trained and tested a DNN regression model with good results. Six months after deployment, the model is performing poorly due to a
 change in the distribution of the input data. How should you address the input differences in production?
option_a: Create alerts to monitor for skew, and retrain the model.
option_b: Perform feature selection on the model, and retrain the model with fewer features.
option_c: Retrain the model, and select an L2 regularization parameter with a hyperparameter tuning service.
option_d: Perform feature selection on the model, and retrain the model on a monthly basis with fewer features.
explanation: A change in the production input distribution is feature drift or training-serving skew. The appropriate response is to monitor and alert on the distribution change, then re-evaluate and retrain the model with representative recent data. Feature selection or regularization alone does not address the changed data distribution.
exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions
topics: Model Monitoring; Hyperparameter Tuning; Regression; Model Optimization

question:
You need to train a computer vision model that predicts the type of government ID present in a given image using a GPU-powered virtual machine
 on Compute
 Engine. You use the following parameters:
 ✑ Optimizer: SGD
 ✑ Image shape = 224ֳ—224
 ✑ Batch size = 64
 ✑ Epochs = 10
 ✑ Verbose =2
 During training you encounter the following error: ResourceExhaustedError: Out Of Memory (OOM) when allocating tensor. What should you do?
option_a: Change the optimizer.
option_b: Reduce the batch size.
option_c: Change the learning rate.
option_d: Reduce the image shape.
explanation: Reducing batch size lowers the number of images and intermediate activations held in GPU memory for each training step, which is the standard first response to an OOM error. Reducing image dimensions could also reduce memory but changes the model input and may hurt accuracy.
exam_objectives: Choosing appropriate hardware for training
topics: Training Hardware; Computer Vision; Evaluation Metrics; Model Optimization

question:
You developed an ML model with AI Platform, and you want to move it to production. You serve a few thousand queries per second and are
 experiencing latency issues. Incoming requests are served by a load balancer that distributes them across multiple Kubeflow CPU-only pods
 running on Google Kubernetes Engine
 (GKE). Your goal is to improve the serving latency without changing the underlying infrastructure. What should you do?
option_a: Significantly increase the max_batch_size TensorFlow Serving parameter.
option_b: Switch to the tensorflow-model-server-universal version of TensorFlow Serving.
option_c: Significantly increase the max_enqueued_batches TensorFlow Serving parameter.
option_d:
Recompile TensorFlow Serving using the source to support CPU-specific optimizations. Instruct GKE to choose an appropriate baseline
 minimum CPU platform for serving nodes.
explanation: The request asks for lower CPU serving latency without changing the overall GKE architecture. A TensorFlow Serving build compiled with CPU-specific optimizations, combined with an appropriate minimum CPU platform, directly improves inference performance. Increasing batching or queue depth can increase throughput but can also worsen tail latency. This is an older question because the named TensorFlow Serving image and AI Platform terminology have changed.
exam_objectives: Scaling online model serving
topics: GKE; Custom Training; Model Optimization; Kubeflow

question:
You have a demand forecasting pipeline in production that uses Dataflow to preprocess raw data prior to model training and prediction. During
 preprocessing, you employ Z-score normalization on data stored in BigQuery and write it back to BigQuery. New training data is added every week.
 You want to make the process more efficient by minimizing computation time and manual intervention. What should you do?
option_a: Translate the normalization algorithm into SQL for use with BigQuery.
option_b: Normalize the data using Google Kubernetes Engine.
option_c: Use the normalizer_fn argument in TensorFlow's Feature Column API.
option_d: Normalize the data with Apache Spark using the Dataproc connector for BigQuery.
explanation: Because the data is already in BigQuery and normalization is a simple aggregate-and-transform operation, translating the Z-score calculation into BigQuery SQL removes the separate Dataflow preprocessing job and minimizes recurring computation and operational work.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: BigQuery; Feature Engineering; Data Preparation; Dataflow

question:
You need to design a customized deep neural network in Keras that will predict customer purchases based on their purchase history. You want to
 explore model performance using multiple model architectures, store training data, and be able to compare the evaluation metrics in the same
 dashboard. What should you do?
option_a: Create multiple models using AutoML Tables.
option_b: Automate multiple training runs using Cloud Composer.
option_c: Run multiple training jobs on AI Platform with similar job names.
option_d: Create an experiment in Kubeflow Pipelines to organize multiple runs.
explanation: Kubeflow Pipelines experiments and runs are designed to organize repeated pipeline executions and compare their parameters and metrics. This matches the need to test multiple Keras architectures and review results together. The terminology is older; Experiments on Agent Platform is the current managed Google Cloud alternative.
terminology_notes: Applied official direct product-name mappings only.

exam_objectives: Tracking and running ML experiments; Developing end-to-end ML pipelines

question:
You are developing a Kubeflow pipeline on Google Kubernetes Engine. The first step in the pipeline is to issue a query against BigQuery. You plan
 to use the results of that query as the input to the next step in your pipeline. You want to achieve this in the easiest way possible. What should you
 do?
option_a: Use the BigQuery console to execute your query, and then save the query results into a new BigQuery table.
option_b:
Write a Python script that uses the BigQuery API to execute queries against BigQuery. Execute this script as the first step in your Kubeflow
 pipeline.
option_c:
Use the Kubeflow Pipelines domain-specific language to create a custom component that uses the Python BigQuery client library to execute
 queries.
option_d:
Locate the Kubeflow Pipelines repository on GitHub. Find the BigQuery Query Component, copy that component's URL, and use it to load the
 component into your pipeline. Use the component to execute queries against BigQuery.
explanation: The easiest approach is to reuse the prebuilt BigQuery query component rather than writing and packaging a custom component. Prebuilt pipeline components reduce code and maintenance. The exact legacy component URL may have changed, so the general principle is to use a supported prebuilt BigQuery pipeline component.
exam_objectives: Developing end-to-end ML pipelines
topics: Kubeflow; BigQuery; Pipelines; GKE

question:
You are building a model to predict daily temperatures. You split the data randomly and then transformed the training and test datasets.
 Temperature data for model training is uploaded hourly. During testing, your model performed with 97% accuracy; however, after deploying to
 production, the model's accuracy dropped to 66%. How can you make your production model more accurate?
option_a: Normalize the data for the training, and test datasets as two separate steps.
option_b: Split the training and test data based on time rather than a random split to avoid leakage.
option_c: Add more data to your test set to ensure that you have a fair distribution and sample for testing.
option_d:
Apply data transformations before splitting, and cross-validate to make sure that the transformations are applied to both the training and
 test sets.
explanation: Hourly temperature observations are time ordered. A random split can put future observations into training while earlier observations appear in testing, producing leakage and an unrealistically high offline score. Split chronologically so validation represents future production data.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: Time Series; Data Preparation; Evaluation Metrics

question:
You are developing models to classify customer support emails. You created models with TensorFlow Estimators using small datasets on your on-
 premises system, but you now need to train the models using large datasets to ensure high performance. You will port your models to Google
 Cloud and want to minimize code refactoring and infrastructure overhead for easier migration from on-prem to cloud. What should you do?
option_a: Use AI Platform for distributed training.
option_b: Create a cluster on Dataproc for training.
option_c: Create a Managed Instance Group with autoscaling.
option_d: Use Kubeflow Pipelines to train on a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster.
explanation: Agent Platform custom training, formerly AI Platform Training, provides managed distributed training and supports TensorFlow training applications with substantially less infrastructure management than Dataproc, managed instance groups, or a self-managed Kubeflow cluster.
terminology_notes: Applied official direct product-name mappings only.
exam_objectives: Training models
topics: Custom Training; Distributed Training; Agents; Dataproc

question:
You have trained a text classification model in TensorFlow using AI Platform. You want to use the trained model for batch predictions on text data
 stored in
 BigQuery while minimizing computational overhead. What should you do?
option_a: Export the model to BigQuery ML.
option_b: Deploy and version the model on AI Platform.
option_c: Use Dataflow with the SavedModel to read the data from BigQuery.
option_d: Submit a batch prediction job on AI Platform that points to the model location in Cloud Storage.
explanation: BigQuery ML can import a TensorFlow SavedModel and run ML.PREDICT directly over BigQuery tables. This avoids exporting the input data or building a separate batch-inference pipeline, which minimizes operational effort.
exam_objectives: Developing ML models using BigQuery ML or AutoML on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
topics: BigQuery ML; Batch Inference; Custom Training; BigQuery

question:
You work with a data engineering team that has developed a pipeline to clean your dataset and save it in a Cloud Storage bucket. You have
 created an ML model and want to use the data to refresh your model as soon as new data is available. As part of your CI/CD workflow, you want to
 automatically run a Kubeflow
 Pipelines training job on Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE). How should you architect this workflow?
option_a: Configure your pipeline with Dataflow, which saves the files in Cloud Storage. After the file is saved, start the training job on a GKE cluster.
option_b:
Use App Engine to create a lightweight python client that continuously polls Cloud Storage for new files. As soon as a file arrives, initiate
 the training job.
option_c:
Configure a Cloud Storage trigger to send a message to a Pub/Sub topic when a new file is available in a storage bucket. Use a Pub/Sub-
 triggered Cloud Function to start the training job on a GKE cluster.
option_d:
Use Cloud Scheduler to schedule jobs at a regular interval. For the first step of the job, check the timestamp of objects in your Cloud
 Storage bucket. If there are no new files since the last run, abort the job.
explanation: A Cloud Storage object-finalize event can publish to Pub/Sub, which can trigger the downstream training workflow as soon as the prepared dataset is written. This is event driven and avoids polling or fixed schedules. Modern implementations commonly use Eventarc or Pub/Sub notifications.
exam_objectives: Automating model retraining; Developing end-to-end ML pipelines
topics: Pipelines; Cloud Storage; Dataflow; Cloud Run

question:
You have a functioning end-to-end ML pipeline that involves tuning the hyperparameters of your ML model using AI Platform, and then using the
 best-tuned parameters for training. Hypertuning is taking longer than expected and is delaying the downstream processes. You want to speed up
 the tuning job without significantly compromising its effectiveness. Which actions should you take? (Choose two.)
option_a: Decrease the number of parallel trials.
option_b: Decrease the range of floating-point values.
option_c: Set the early stopping parameter to TRUE.
option_d: Change the search algorithm from Bayesian search to random search.
option_e: Decrease the maximum number of trials during subsequent training phases.
explanation: Early stopping terminates unpromising hyperparameter trials, and reducing the maximum number of trials in later tuning phases directly reduces cost. Reducing parallelism mainly changes elapsed time, and narrowing ranges can miss the optimum. This question is somewhat ambiguous because cost and wall-clock time can trade off differently.
exam_objectives: Training models; Choosing appropriate hardware for training
topics: Hyperparameter Tuning; Pipelines; Custom Training

question:
Your team is building an application for a global bank that will be used by millions of customers. You built a forecasting model that predicts
 customers' account balances 3 days in the future. Your team will use the results in a new feature that will notify users when their account balance
 is likely to drop below $25. How should you serve your predictions?
option_a:
1. Create a Pub/Sub topic for each user. 2. Deploy a Cloud Function that sends a notification when your model predicts that a user's
 account balance will drop below the $25 threshold.
option_b:
1. Create a Pub/Sub topic for each user. 2. Deploy an application on the App Engine standard environment that sends a notification when
 your model predicts that a user's account balance will drop below the $25 threshold.
option_c:
1. Build a notification system on Firebase. 2. Register each user with a user ID on the Firebase Cloud Messaging server, which sends a
 notification when the average of all account balance predictions drops below the $25 threshold.
option_d:
1. Build a notification system on Firebase. 2. Register each user with a user ID on the Firebase Cloud Messaging server, which sends a
 notification when your model predicts that a user's account balance will drop below the $25 threshold.
explanation: Firebase Cloud Messaging is designed to send notifications to millions of registered client devices. Each user should receive a notification based on that user's predicted balance, not a global average, so option D matches the requirement.
exam_objectives: Serving models
topics: Forecasting; Cloud Run; Online Inference

question:
You work for an advertising company and want to understand the effectiveness of your company's latest advertising campaign. You have
 streamed 500 MB of campaign data into BigQuery. You want to query the table, and then manipulate the results of that query with a pandas
 dataframe in an AI Platform notebook.
 What should you do?
option_a: Use AI Platform Notebooks' BigQuery cell magic to query the data, and ingest the results as a pandas dataframe.
option_b: Export your table as a CSV file from BigQuery to Google Drive, and use the Google Drive API to ingest the file into your notebook instance.
option_c:
Download your table from BigQuery as a local CSV file, and upload it to your AI Platform notebook instance. Use pandas.read_csv to ingest
 he file as a pandas dataframe.
option_d:
From a bash cell in your AI Platform notebook, use the bq extract command to export the table as a CSV file to Cloud Storage, and then use
 gsutil cp to copy the data into the notebook. Use pandas.read_csv to ingest the file as a pandas dataframe.
explanation: BigQuery notebook integrations let the analyst query BigQuery directly from the managed notebook and continue analysis in the same environment. Exporting and downloading CSV files creates unnecessary copies and manual steps.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Model prototyping using notebooks
topics: Workbench; BigQuery; Cloud Storage

question:
You are an ML engineer at a global car manufacture. You need to build an ML model to predict car sales in different cities around the world. Which
 features or feature crosses should you use to train city-specific relationships between car type and number of sales?
option_a: Thee individual features: binned latitude, binned longitude, and one-hot encoded car type.
option_b: One feature obtained as an element-wise product between latitude, longitude, and car type.
option_c: One feature obtained as an element-wise product between binned latitude, binned longitude, and one-hot encoded car type.
option_d:
Two feature crosses as an element-wise product: the first between binned latitude and one-hot encoded car type, and the second between
 binned longitude and one-hot encoded car type.
explanation: Binning latitude and longitude creates discrete geographic cells, and crossing those buckets with the one-hot encoded car type lets the model learn car-type-specific local effects. Multiplying raw continuous coordinates is not an appropriate categorical feature cross.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: Feature Engineering; Data Preparation

question:
You work for a large technology company that wants to modernize their contact center. You have been asked to develop a solution to classify
 incoming calls by product so that requests can be more quickly routed to the correct support team. You have already transcribed the calls using
 the Speech-to-Text API. You want to minimize data preprocessing and development time. How should you build the model?
option_a: Use the AI Platform Training built-in algorithms to create a custom model.
option_b: Use AutoMlL Natural Language to extract custom entities for classification.
option_c: Use the Cloud Natural Language API to extract custom entities for classification.
option_d:
Build a custom model to identify the product keywords from the transcribed calls, and then run the keywords through a classification
 algorithm.
explanation: A custom entity extraction model can identify product names in call transcripts with minimal custom model engineering. The standard Natural Language API does not train organization-specific entity types, while AutoML Natural Language, now Vertex AI text entity extraction, supports custom entities. The wording says classification, but the options focus on entity extraction, so this item is imperfect.
terminology_notes: Generic or unrecognized Vertex AI reference requires contextual review.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models
topics: NLP; AutoML; Classification; Speech-to-Text

question:
You are training a TensorFlow model on a structured dataset with 100 billion records stored in several CSV files. You need to improve the
 input/output execution performance. What should you do?
option_a: Load the data into BigQuery, and read the data from BigQuery.
option_b: Load the data into Cloud Bigtable, and read the data from Bigtable.
option_c: Convert the CSV files into shards of TFRecords, and store the data in Cloud Storage.
option_d: Convert the CSV files into shards of TFRecords, and store the data in the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS).
explanation: TFRecord is TensorFlow's optimized record format. Sharding TFRecord files enables parallel reads and avoids the parsing overhead and poor access patterns associated with very large CSV collections. The number and size of shards should be tuned to the training setup.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: Data Preparation; Pipelines; BigQuery; Cloud Storage

question:
As the lead ML Engineer for your company, you are responsible for building ML models to digitize scanned customer forms. You have developed a
 TensorFlow model that converts the scanned images into text and stores them in Cloud Storage. You need to use your ML model on the
 aggregated data collected at the end of each day with minimal manual intervention. What should you do?
option_a: Use the batch prediction functionality of AI Platform.
option_b: Create a serving pipeline in Compute Engine for prediction.
option_c: Use Cloud Functions for prediction each time a new data point is ingested.
option_d: Deploy the model on AI Platform and create a version of it for online inference.
explanation: The input is a large collection of existing scanned forms, so managed batch prediction is the appropriate serving mode. It provides scalable offline inference without maintaining an always-on endpoint or custom serving fleet.
exam_objectives: Serving models
topics: Batch Inference; Cloud Storage; Computer Vision; Cloud Run

question:
You recently joined an enterprise-scale company that has thousands of datasets. You know that there are accurate descriptions for each table in
 BigQuery, and you are searching for the proper BigQuery table to use for a model you are building on AI Platform. How should you find the data
 that you need?
option_a: Use Data Catalog to search the BigQuery datasets by using keywords in the table description.
option_b: Tag each of your model and version resources on AI Platform with the name of the BigQuery table that was used for training.
option_c:
Maintain a lookup table in BigQuery that maps the table descriptions to the table ID. Query the lookup table to find the correct table ID for
 the data that you need.
option_d:
Execute a query in BigQuery to retrieve all the existing table names in your project using the INFORMATION_SCHEMA metadata tables that
 are native to BigQuery. Use the result o find the table that you need.
explanation: Data Catalog, now part of Dataplex Universal Catalog, indexes BigQuery metadata such as table descriptions and supports keyword search across datasets. This is more scalable than maintaining a manual lookup table.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: ML Metadata; BigQuery; Data Preparation

question:
You started working on a classification problem with time series data and achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC
 ROC) value of
 99% for training data after just a few experiments. You haven't explored using any sophisticated algorithms or spent any time on hyperparameter
 tuning. What should your next step be to identify and fix the problem?
option_a: Address the model overfitting by using a less complex algorithm.
option_b: Address data leakage by applying nested cross-validation during model training.
option_c: Address data leakage by removing features highly correlated with the target value.
option_d: Address the model overfitting by tuning the hyperparameters to reduce the AUC ROC value.
explanation: A nearly perfect score after only a few experiments is a warning sign for leakage. Features that directly reveal or are created after the target event must be removed. Nested cross-validation does not fix leakage if leaked features remain. The phrase 'highly correlated' is not sufficient by itself, so the real check is whether the feature contains target or future information.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: Data Preparation; Time Series; Evaluation Metrics; Experiments

question:
You work for an online travel agency that also sells advertising placements on its website to other companies. You have been asked to predict the
 most relevant web banner that a user should see next. Security is important to your company. The model latency requirements are 300ms@p99,
 the inventory is thousands of web banners, and your exploratory analysis has shown that navigation context is a good predictor. You want to
 Implement the simplest solution. How should you configure the prediction pipeline?
option_a: Embed the client on the website, and then deploy the model on AI Platform Prediction.
option_b: Embed the client on the website, deploy the gateway on App Engine, and then deploy the model on AI Platform Prediction.
option_c:
Embed the client on the website, deploy the gateway on App Engine, deploy the database on Cloud Bigtable for writing and for reading the
 user's navigation context, and then deploy the model on AI Platform Prediction.
option_d:
Embed the client on the website, deploy the gateway on App Engine, deploy the database on Memorystore for writing and for reading the
 user's navigation context, and then deploy the model on Google Kubernetes Engine.
explanation: The solution needs a secure server-side gateway, low-latency access to a large and frequently updated navigation context, and managed online prediction. Cloud Bigtable is designed for high-throughput, low-latency key-based reads and writes at scale. This question is dated and the simplest modern design might also consider Firestore or Memorystore depending on data size and access patterns.
exam_objectives: Scaling online model serving; Identifying risks to AI solutions
topics: Online Inference; AI Security; GKE; Pipelines

question:
Your team is building a convolutional neural network (CNN)-based architecture from scratch. The preliminary experiments running on your on-
 premises CPU-only infrastructure were encouraging, but have slow convergence. You have been asked to speed up model training to reduce time-
 to-market. You want to experiment with virtual machines (VMs) on Google Cloud to leverage more powerful hardware. Your code does not include
 any manual device placement and has not been wrapped in Estimator model-level abstraction. Which environment should you train your model on?
option_a: AVM on Compute Engine and 1 TPU with all dependencies installed manually.
option_b: AVM on Compute Engine and 8 GPUs with all dependencies installed manually.
option_c: A Deep Learning VM with an n1-standard-2 machine and 1 GPU with all libraries pre-installed.
option_d: A Deep Learning VM with more powerful CPU e2-highcpu-16 machines with all libraries pre-installed.
explanation: A Deep Learning VM provides preinstalled ML frameworks and GPU drivers, minimizing setup effort. A single GPU is the least costly listed accelerator for initial CNN experiments; eight GPUs or a TPU are unnecessary before the architecture has been validated.
exam_objectives: Choosing appropriate hardware for training
topics: Training Hardware; Experiments

question:
You work on a growing team of more than 50 data scientists who all use AI Platform. You are designing a strategy to organize your jobs, models,
 and versions in a clean and scalable way. Which strategy should you choose?
option_a: Set up restrictive IAM permissions on the AI Platform notebooks so that only a single user or group can access a given instance.
option_b:
Separate each data scientist's work into a different project to ensure that the jobs, models, and versions created by each data scientist are
 accessible only to that user.
option_c:
Use labels to organize resources into descriptive categories. Apply a label to each created resource so that users can filter the results by
 label when viewing or monitoring the resources.
option_d:
Set up a BigQuery sink for Cloud Logging logs that is appropriately filtered to capture information about AI Platform resource usage. In
 BigQuery, create a SQL view that maps users to the resources they are using
explanation: Labels are the standard way to organize Google Cloud resources by team, experiment, environment, or owner without creating a separate project for every data scientist. They also support filtering and cost reporting.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Tracking and running ML experiments
topics: IAM; BigQuery; Workbench; Experiments

question:
You are training a deep learning model for semantic image segmentation with reduced training time. While using a Deep Learning VM Image, you
 receive the following error: The resource 'projects/deeplearning-platforn/zones/europe-west4-c/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-k80' was not found.
 What should you do?
option_a: Ensure that you have GPU quota in the selected region.
option_b: Ensure that the required GPU is available in the selected region.
option_c: Ensure that you have preemptible GPU quota in the selected region.
option_d: Ensure that the selected GPU has enough GPU memory for the workload.
explanation: The error states that the requested GPU type is unavailable in the selected zone or region. Quota and memory are separate issues. Choose a location where that accelerator is offered or select a different supported accelerator.
exam_objectives: Choosing appropriate hardware for training
topics: Training Hardware; Clustering; Computer Vision

question:
Your team is working on an NLP research project to predict political affiliation of authors based on articles they have written. You have a large
 training dataset that is structured like this:
 You followed the standard 80%-10%-10% data distribution across the training, testing, and evaluation subsets. How should you distribute the
 training examples across the train-test-eval subsets while maintaining the 80-10-10 proportion?
option_a:
Distribute texts randomly across the train-test-eval subsets: Train set: [TextA1, TextB2, ...] Test set: [TextA2, TextC1, TextD2, ...] Eval set:
 [TextB1, TextC2, TextD1, ...]
option_b:
Distribute authors randomly across the train-test-eval subsets: (*) Train set: [TextA1, TextA2, TextD1, TextD2, ...] Test set: [TextB1, TextB2,
 ...] Eval set: [TexC1,TextC2 ...]
option_c:
Distribute sentences randomly across the train-test-eval subsets: Train set: [SentenceA11, SentenceA21, SentenceB11, SentenceB21,
 SentenceC11, SentenceD21 ...] Test set: [SentenceA12, SentenceA22, SentenceB12, SentenceC22, SentenceC12, SentenceD22 ...] Eval set:
 [SentenceA13, SentenceA23, SentenceB13, SentenceC23, SentenceC13, SentenceD31 ...]
option_d:
Distribute paragraphs of texts (i.e., chunks of consecutive sentences) across the train-test-eval subsets: Train set: [SentenceA11,
 SentenceA12, SentenceD11, SentenceD12 ...] Test set: [SentenceA13, SentenceB13, SentenceB21, SentenceD23, SentenceC12, SentenceD13
 ...] Eval set: [SentenceA11, SentenceA22, SentenceB13, SentenceD22, SentenceC23, SentenceD11 ...]
explanation: The prediction target is an author's political affiliation, so all articles from one author must stay in the same split. Randomly splitting authors prevents the model from seeing the same author's writing style in both training and evaluation, which would leak identity information.

question:
Your team has been tasked with creating an ML solution in Google Cloud to classify support requests for one of your platforms. You analyzed the
 requirements and decided to use TensorFlow to build the classifier so that you have full control of the model's code, serving, and deployment. You
 will use Kubeflow pipelines for the ML platform. To save time, you want to build on existing resources and use managed services instead of
 building a completely new model. How should you build the classifier?
option_a: Use the Natural Language API to classify support requests.
option_b: Use AutoML Natural Language to build the support requests classifier.
option_c: Use an established text classification model on AI Platform to perform transfer learning.
option_d: Use an established text classification model on AI Platform as-is to classify support requests.
explanation: The requirement is to retain TensorFlow code and deployment control while avoiding a model built entirely from scratch. Starting from an established pretrained text-classification model and fine-tuning it is transfer learning and fits a Kubeflow-based custom pipeline. The former AI Platform model resources are now typically sourced from TensorFlow Hub or Model Garden and trained on Vertex AI.

question:
You recently joined a machine learning team that will soon release a new project. As a lead on the project, you are asked to determine the
 production readiness of the ML components. The team has already tested features and data, model development, and infrastructure. Which
 additional readiness check should you recommend to the team?
option_a: Ensure that training is reproducible.
option_b: Ensure that all hyperparameters are tuned.
option_c: Ensure that model performance is monitored.
option_d: Ensure that feature expectations are captured in the schema.
explanation: A production-readiness review must include post-deployment monitoring so the team can detect drift, skew, latency problems, and model-quality degradation. The question says feature/data, development, and infrastructure checks are already complete, making monitoring the missing lifecycle control.
exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions; Developing end-to-end ML pipelines
topics: Model Monitoring; Hyperparameter Tuning; Troubleshooting

question:
You work for a credit card company and have been asked to create a custom fraud detection model based on historical data using AutoML Tables.
 You need to prioritize detection of fraudulent transactions while minimizing false positives. Which optimization objective should you use when
 training the model?
option_a: An optimization objective that minimizes Log loss
option_b: An optimization objective that maximizes the Precision at a Recall value of 0.50
option_c: An optimization objective that maximizes the area under the precision-recall curve (AUC PR) value
option_d: An optimization objective that maximizes the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC ROC) value
explanation: Fraud is a rare positive class, so AUC PR is more informative than AUC ROC across class imbalance and balances precision and recall across thresholds. Precision at recall 0.50 fixes recall at a low value and may miss too many fraudulent transactions.
exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions
topics: Evaluation Metrics; Data Preparation; Classification; AutoML

question:
Your company manages a video sharing website where users can watch and upload videos. You need to create an ML model to predict which
 newly uploaded videos will be the most popular so that those videos can be prioritized on your company's website. Which result should you use to
 determine whether the model is successful?
option_a: The model predicts videos as popular if the user who uploads them has over 10,000 likes.
option_b: The model predicts 97.5% of the most popular clickbait videos measured by number of clicks.
option_c: The model predicts 95% of the most popular videos measured by watch time within 30 days of being uploaded.
option_d: The Pearson correlation coefficient between the log-transformed number of views after 7 days and 30 days after publication is equal to 0.
explanation: The success metric should measure the actual business definition of popularity. Watch time within a defined period is more meaningful than uploader likes or raw clickbait clicks, and a 95% capture rate is a clear measurable target.
exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions
topics: Evaluation Metrics; Recommendation Systems; Model Monitoring

question:
You are working on a Neural Network-based project. The dataset provided to you has columns with different ranges. While preparing the data for
 model training, you discover that gradient optimization is having difficulty moving weights to a good solution. What should you do?
option_a: Use feature construction to combine the strongest features.
option_b: Use the representation transformation (normalization) technique.
option_c: Improve the data cleaning step by removing features with missing values.
option_d: Change the partitioning step to reduce the dimension of the test set and have a larger training set.
explanation: When input features have very different scales, gradient-based optimization can move inefficiently through the loss surface. Normalization puts features on comparable scales and generally improves convergence.

question:
Your data science team needs to rapidly experiment with various features, model architectures, and hyperparameters. They need to track the
 accuracy metrics for various experiments and use an API to query the metrics over time. What should they use to track and report their
 experiments while minimizing manual effort?
option_a: Use Kubeflow Pipelines to execute the experiments. Export the metrics file, and query the results using the Kubeflow Pipelines API.
option_b: Use AI Platform Training to execute the experiments. Write the accuracy metrics to BigQuery, and query the results using the BigQuery API.
option_c:
Use AI Platform Training to execute the experiments. Write the accuracy metrics to Cloud Monitoring, and query the results using the
 Monitoring API.
option_d:
Use AI Platform Notebooks to execute the experiments. Collect the results in a shared Google Sheets file, and query the results using the
 Google Sheets API.
explanation: Kubeflow Pipelines records run parameters, artifacts, and scalar metrics and exposes them through its API, so experiments can be compared with little custom tracking code. The current fully managed Google Cloud equivalent is Experiments on Agent Platform and Agent Platform ML Metadata.

question:
You work for a bank and are building a random forest model for fraud detection. You have a dataset that includes transactions, of which 1% are
 identified as fraudulent. Which data transformation strategy would likely improve the performance of your classifier?
option_a: Write your data in TFRecords.
option_b: Z-normalize all the numeric features.
option_c: Oversample the fraudulent transaction 10 times.
option_d: Use one-hot encoding on all categorical features.
explanation: With only 1% fraudulent examples, oversampling the minority class gives the classifier more fraud examples during training and can improve its ability to learn the rare class. TFRecord format and normalization do not directly address class imbalance.

question:
You are using transfer learning to train an image classifier based on a pre-trained EfficientNet model. Your training dataset has 20,000 images.
 You plan to retrain the model once per day. You need to minimize the cost of infrastructure. What platform components and configuration
 environment should you use?
option_a: A Deep Learning VM with 4 V100 GPUs and local storage.
option_b: A Deep Learning VM with 4 V100 GPUs and Cloud Storage.
option_c: A Google Kubernetes Engine cluster with a V100 GPU Node Pool and an NFS Server
option_d: An AI Platform Training job using a custom scale tier with 4 V100 GPUs and Cloud Storage
explanation: A managed custom training job provisions the requested GPUs only for the daily run and shuts them down afterward, avoiding the idle cost and maintenance of persistent VMs or GKE infrastructure. Cloud Storage provides durable shared input and model storage. Four V100 GPUs may still be excessive, but D is the best listed managed, ephemeral option.

topics: Custom Training; Training Hardware; Cloud Storage; GKE

question:
While conducting an exploratory analysis of a dataset, you discover that categorical feature A has substantial predictive power, but it is
 sometimes missing. What should you do?
option_a: Drop feature A if more than 15% of values are missing. Otherwise, use feature A as-is.
option_b: Compute the mode of feature A and then use it to replace the missing values in feature A.
option_c: Replace the missing values with the values of the feature with the highest Pearson correlation with feature A.
option_d: Add an additional class to categorical feature A for missing values. Create a new binary feature that indicates whether feature A is missing.
explanation: For a predictive categorical feature, treating missing as its own category preserves the row and can capture informative missingness. A separate missingness indicator gives the model an explicit signal. Mode imputation can blur meaningful differences.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: Feature Engineering; Data Preparation

question:
You work for a large retailer and have been asked to segment your customers by their purchasing habits. The purchase history of all customers
 has been uploaded to BigQuery. You suspect that there may be several distinct customer segments, however you are unsure of how many, and you
 don’t yet understand the commonalities in their behavior. You want to find the most efficient solution. What should you do?
option_a: Create a k-means clustering model using BigQuery ML. Allow BigQuery to automatically optimize the number of clusters.
option_b: Create a new dataset in Dataprep that references your BigQuery table. Use Dataprep to identify similarities within each column.
option_c:
Use the Data Labeling Service to label each customer record in BigQuery. Train a model on your labeled data using AutoML Tables. Review
 the evaluation metrics to understand whether there is an underlying pattern in the data.
option_d:
Get a list of the customer segments from your company’s Marketing team. Use the Data Labeling Service to label each customer record in
 BigQuery according to the list. Analyze the distribution of labels in your dataset using Data Studio.
explanation: This is an unsupervised segmentation problem. BigQuery ML k-means trains directly on the BigQuery data and can use automatic hyperparameter tuning for the number of clusters, avoiding data movement and manual labeling.
exam_objectives: Developing ML models using BigQuery ML or AutoML on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
topics: BigQuery ML; Clustering; Hyperparameter Tuning; AutoML

question:
You recently designed and built a custom neural network that uses critical dependencies specific to your organization’s framework. You need to
 train the model using a managed training service on Google Cloud. However, the ML framework and related dependencies are not supported by AI
 Platform Training. Also, both your model and your data are too large to fit in memory on a single machine. Your ML framework of choice uses the
 scheduler, workers, and servers distribution structure. What should you do?
option_a: Use a built-in model available on AI Platform Training.
option_b: Build your custom container to run jobs on AI Platform Training.
option_c: Build your custom containers to run distributed training jobs on AI Platform Training.
option_d: Reconfigure your code to a ML framework with dependencies that are supported by AI Platform Training.
explanation: The framework and dependencies require custom containers, and the model cannot fit on one machine, so the training job must be distributed across worker pools. Agent Platform custom training supports custom containers and distributed worker-pool specifications.

question:
While monitoring your model training’s GPU utilization, you discover that you have a native synchronous implementation. The training data is split
 into multiple files. You want to reduce the execution time of your input pipeline. What should you do?
option_a: Increase the CPU load
option_b: Add caching to the pipeline
option_c: Increase the network bandwidth
option_d: Add parallel interleave to the pipeline
explanation: When training data is spread across many files, parallel interleave reads multiple files concurrently and reduces input stalls that leave the GPU idle. Caching helps repeated epochs only when the dataset or transformed data fits the cache.
exam_objectives: Training models
topics: Pipelines; Training Hardware; Model Optimization; Data Preparation

question:
Your data science team is training a PyTorch model for image classification based on a pre-trained RestNet model. You need to perform
 hyperparameter tuning to optimize for several parameters. What should you do?
option_a: Convert the model to a Keras model, and run a Keras Tuner job.
option_b: Run a hyperparameter tuning job on AI Platform using custom containers.
option_c: Create a Kuberflow Pipelines instance, and run a hyperparameter tuning job on Katib.
option_d: Convert the model to a TensorFlow model, and run a hyperparameter tuning job on AI Platform.
explanation: Vertex AI hyperparameter tuning can run a PyTorch training application in a custom container, so no framework conversion is required. Katib is possible on Kubeflow but adds cluster and platform management.

question:
You have a large corpus of written support cases that can be classified into 3 separate categories: Technical Support, Billing Support, or Other
 Issues. You need to quickly build, test, and deploy a service that will automatically classify future written requests into one of the categories. How
 should you configure the pipeline?
option_a: Use the Cloud Natural Language API to obtain metadata to classify the incoming cases.
option_b: Use AutoML Natural Language to build and test a classifier. Deploy the model as a REST API.
option_c: Use BigQuery ML to build and test a logistic regression model to classify incoming requests. Use BigQuery ML to perform inference.
option_d: Create a TensorFlow model using Google’s BERT pre-trained model. Build and test a classifier, and deploy the model using Vertex AI.
explanation: A managed custom text-classification service is the fastest way to train, evaluate, deploy, and expose a three-class classifier without building the full NLP stack. AutoML Natural Language has been superseded by Vertex AI text classification, but the architectural answer remains B.
terminology_notes: Generic or unrecognized Vertex AI reference requires contextual review.

question:
You need to quickly build and train a model to predict the sentiment of customer reviews with custom categories without writing code. You do not
 have enough data to train a model from scratch. The resulting model should have high predictive performance. Which service should you use?
option_a: AutoML Natural Language
option_b: Cloud Natural Language API
option_c: AI Hub pre-made Jupyter Notebooks
option_d: AI Platform Training built-in algorithms
explanation: Custom sentiment categories require a custom classifier rather than the fixed sentiment output of the Natural Language API. AutoML Natural Language, now Vertex AI text classification, provides a no-code training path and transfer-learning-based performance with less data than training from scratch.

question:
You need to build an ML model for a social media application to predict whether a user’s submitted profile photo meets the requirements. The
 application will inform the user if the picture meets the requirements. How should you build a model to ensure that the application does not
 falsely accept a non-compliant picture?
option_a: Use AutoML to optimize the model’s recall in order to minimize false negatives.
option_b: Use AutoML to optimize the model’s F1 score in order to balance the accuracy of false positives and false negatives.
option_c:
Use Agent Platform Workbench user-managed notebooks to build a custom model that has three times as many examples of pictures that meet
 the profile photo requirements.
option_d:
Use Agent Platform Workbench user-managed notebooks to build a custom model that has three times as many examples of pictures that do not
 meet the profile photo requirements.
explanation: Assuming the positive class is 'non-compliant,' falsely accepting a bad photo is a false negative. Optimizing recall for the non-compliant class reduces false negatives. The question is ambiguous because it never explicitly defines which class is positive; that class definition must be confirmed in a real implementation.

question:
You lead a data science team at a large international corporation. Most of the models your team trains are large-scale models using high-level
 TensorFlow APIs on AI Platform with GPUs. Your team usually takes a few weeks or months to iterate on a new version of a model. You were
 recently asked to review your team’s spending. How should you reduce your Google Cloud compute costs without impacting the model’s
 performance?
option_a: Use AI Platform to run distributed training jobs with checkpoints.
option_b: Use AI Platform to run distributed training jobs without checkpoints.
option_c: Migrate to training with Kuberflow on Google Kubernetes Engine, and use preemptible VMs with checkpoints.
option_d: Migrate to training with Kuberflow on Google Kubernetes Engine, and use preemptible VMs without checkpoints.
explanation: Preemptible, now Spot, VMs reduce compute cost, and checkpointing allows long-running distributed jobs to resume after a VM is reclaimed. The migration to self-managed Kubeflow adds operational overhead, but among the listed options it is the only one that combines discounted capacity with fault recovery.

question:
You need to train a regression model based on a dataset containing 50,000 records that is stored in BigQuery. The data includes a total of 20
 categorical and numerical features with a target variable that can include negative values. You need to minimize effort and training time while
 maximizing model performance. What approach should you take to train this regression model?
option_a: Create a custom TensorFlow DNN model
option_b: Use BQML XGBoost regression to train the model.
option_c: Use AutoML Tables to train the model without early stopping.
option_d: Use AutoML Tables to train the model with RMSLE as the optimization objective.
explanation: BigQuery ML boosted-tree regression trains directly where the 50,000-row dataset resides, requires little code, handles mixed feature types, and is compatible with negative target values. RMSLE is unsuitable when labels can be negative.
exam_objectives: Developing ML models using BigQuery ML or AutoML on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
topics: BigQuery ML; Regression; AutoML; BigQuery

question:
You are building a linear model with over 100 input features, all with values between –1 and 1. You suspect that many features are non-
 informative. You want to remove the non-informative features from your model while keeping the informative ones in their original form. Which
 technique should you use?
option_a: Use L1 regularization to reduce the coefficients of uninformative features to 0.
option_b: Use principal component analysis (PCA) to eliminate the least informative features.
option_c: After building your model, use Shapley values to determine which features are the most informative.
option_d: Use an iterative dropout technique to identify which features do not degrade the model when removed.
explanation: L1 regularization encourages sparse linear-model coefficients by driving weak or uninformative feature weights exactly to zero while leaving retained features in their original representation. PCA would replace the original features with components.
exam_objectives: Training models
topics: Model Optimization; Custom Training

question:
You work for a global footwear retailer and need to predict when an item will be out of stock based on historical inventory data Customer behavior
 is highly dynamic since footwear demand is influenced by many different factors. You want to serve models that are trained on all available data,
 but track your performance on specific subsets of data before pushing to production. What is the most streamlined and reliable way to perform
 this validation?
option_a: Use then TFX ModelValidator tools to specify performance metrics for production readiness.
option_b: Use k-fold cross-validation as a validation strategy to ensure that your model is ready for production.
option_c: Use the last relevant week of data as a validation set to ensure that your model is performing accurately on current data.
option_d: Use the entire dataset and treat the area under the receiver operating characteristics curve (AUC ROC) as the main metric.
explanation: A model-validation component can evaluate a candidate model against defined metrics and compare it with the currently blessed model before deployment. This is more streamlined than manually holding out one recent week or using a generic metric without production thresholds. The legacy TFX ModelValidator functionality is now largely represented by Evaluator and model validation/blessing patterns.
exam_objectives: Developing end-to-end ML pipelines; Automating model retraining
topics: Evaluation Metrics; Pipelines; TFX; Time Series

question:
You have deployed a model on Vertex AI for real-time inference. During an online prediction request, you get an “Out of Memory” error. What
 should you do?
option_a: Use batch prediction mode instead of online mode.
option_b: Send the request again with a smaller batch of instances.
option_c: Use base64 to encode your data before using it for prediction.
option_d: Apply for a quota increase for the number of prediction requests.
explanation: Online prediction request memory grows with the number and size of instances in one request. Retrying with a smaller batch reduces per-request memory. Batch prediction changes the serving mode and is not necessary for an otherwise valid real-time use case.
terminology_notes: Generic or unrecognized Vertex AI reference requires contextual review.
exam_objectives: Scaling online model serving
topics: Online Inference; Batch Inference; Troubleshooting

question:
You work at a subscription-based company. You have trained an ensemble of trees and neural networks to predict customer churn, which is the
 likelihood that customers will not renew their yearly subscription. The average prediction is a 15% churn rate, but for a particular customer the
 model predicts that they are 70% likely to churn. The customer has a product usage history of 30%, is located in New York City, and became a
 customer in 1997. You need to explain the difference between the actual prediction, a 70% churn rate, and the average prediction. You want to use
 Vertex Explainable AI. What should you do?
option_a: Train local surrogate models to explain individual predictions.
option_b: Configure sampled Shapley explanations on Vertex Explainable AI.
option_c: Configure integrated gradients explanations on Vertex Explainable AI.
option_d: Measure the effect of each feature as the weight of the feature multiplied by the feature value.
explanation: Sampled Shapley is appropriate for feature attribution on tabular or mixed-feature models, including tree and neural-network ensembles. It explains how each feature moves an individual prediction away from a baseline such as the average prediction.
exam_objectives: Identifying risks to AI solutions
topics: Explainability; Classification; Responsible AI

question:
You are working on a classification problem with time series data. After conducting just a few experiments using random cross-validation, you
 achieved an Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve (AUC ROC) value of 99% on the training data. You haven’t explored using any
 sophisticated algorithms or spent any time on hyperparameter tuning. What should your next step be to identify and fix the problem?
option_a: Address the model overfitting by using a less complex algorithm and use k-fold cross-validation.
option_b: Address data leakage by applying nested cross-validation during model training.
option_c: Address data leakage by removing features highly correlated with the target value.
option_d: Address the model overfitting by tuning the hyperparameters to reduce the AUC ROC value.
explanation: A suspiciously high result with random cross-validation on time-series data suggests leakage, especially from target-derived or future-looking features. Those features must be identified and removed. None of the options proposes time-based validation, which would also be required, so C is the best available but incomplete answer.

question:
You need to execute a batch prediction on 100 million records in a BigQuery table with a custom TensorFlow DNN regressor model, and then store
 the predicted results in a BigQuery table. You want to minimize the effort required to build this inference pipeline. What should you do?
option_a: Import the TensorFlow model with BigQuery ML, and run the ml.predict function.
option_b: Use the TensorFlow BigQuery reader to load the data, and use the BigQuery API to write the results to BigQuery.
option_c:
Create a Dataflow pipeline to convert the data in BigQuery to TFRecords. Run a batch inference on Vertex AI Prediction, and write the
 results to BigQuery.
option_d:
Load the TensorFlow SavedModel in a Dataflow pipeline. Use the BigQuery I/O connector with a custom function to perform the inference
 within the pipeline, and write the results to BigQuery.
explanation: BigQuery ML can import a TensorFlow SavedModel and apply ML.PREDICT to a BigQuery table, writing the results with a SQL query. This is substantially simpler than building Dataflow and Vertex AI batch-inference plumbing for 100 million rows.

question:
You are creating a deep neural network classification model using a dataset with categorical input values. Certain columns have a cardinality
 greater than 10,000 unique values. How should you encode these categorical values as input into the model?
option_a: Convert each categorical value into an integer value.
option_b: Convert the categorical string data to one-hot hash buckets.
option_c: Map the categorical variables into a vector of boolean values.
option_d: Convert each categorical value into a run-length encoded string.
explanation: One-hot encoding 10,000-plus categories directly would create an extremely large sparse feature space. Hashing categorical strings into a fixed number of buckets bounds the dimensionality and handles unseen values, though learned embeddings may be preferable in a modern deep model.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
