question:
You are developing an ML model using a dataset with categorical input variables. You have randomly split half of the data into training and test
 sets. After applying one-hot encoding on the categorical variables in the training set, you discover that one categorical variable is missing from
 the test set. What should you do?
option_a: Use sparse representation in the test set.
option_b: Randomly redistribute the data, with 70% for the training set and 30% for the test set
option_c: Apply one-hot encoding on the categorical variables in the test data
option_d: Collect more data representing all categories
explanation: The test set must be transformed with the same vocabulary and one-hot mapping learned from the training set. A category absent from test data simply produces an all-zero value for that category's column; the encoder should not be fit independently on the test set. Option C is closest, but the fitted training encoder must be reused.

question:
You work for a bank and are building a random forest model for fraud detection. You have a dataset that includes transactions, of which 1% are
 identified as fraudulent. Which data transformation strategy would likely improve the performance of your classifier?
option_a: Modify the target variable using the Box-Cox transformation.
option_b: Z-normalize all the numeric features.
option_c: Oversample the fraudulent transaction 10 times.
option_d: Log transform all numeric features.
explanation: Oversampling the 1% fraudulent class gives the model more minority examples during training and directly addresses class imbalance. Numeric normalization or log transforms may help optimization but do not solve the rare-class representation problem.

question:
You are developing a classification model to support predictions for your company’s various products. The dataset you were given for model
 development has class imbalance You need to minimize false positives and false negatives What evaluation metric should you use to properly
 train the model?
option_a: F1 score
option_b: Recall
option_c: Accuracy
option_d: Precision
explanation: F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall and is appropriate when the goal is to balance false positives and false negatives on an imbalanced classification problem. Accuracy can remain high while minority-class performance is poor.

question:
You are training an object detection machine learning model on a dataset that consists of three million X-ray images, each roughly 2 GB in size.
 You are using Agent Platform Managed Training to run a custom training application on a Compute Engine instance with 32-cores, 128 GB of RAM, and 1 NVIDIA
 P100 GPU. You notice that model training is taking a very long time. You want to decrease training time without sacrificing model performance.
 What should you do?
option_a: Increase the instance memory to 512 GB, and increase the batch size.
option_b: Replace the NVIDIA P100 GPU with a K80 GPU in the training job.
option_c: Enable early stopping in your Agent Platform Managed Training job.
option_d: Use the tf.distribute.Strategy API and run a distributed training job.

question:

 training and validation losses barely changed during the training run. You want to quickly debug your model. What should you do first?
option_a: Verify that your model can obtain a low loss on a small subset of the dataset
option_b: Add handcrafted features to inject your domain knowledge into the model
option_c: Use the Vertex AI hyperparameter tuning service to identify a better learning rate
option_d: Use hardware accelerators and train your model for more epochs

 consumption in the company’s manufacturing plants based on sensor data collected from all of the plants. The sensors collect tens of millions of
 records every day. You need to schedule daily training runs for your model that use all the data collected up to the current date. You want your
 model to scale smoothly and require minimal development work. What should you do?
option_a: Develop a regression model using BigQuery ML.
option_b: Develop a custom TensorFlow regression model, and optimize it using Agent Platform Managed Training.
option_c: Develop a custom scikit-learn regression model, and optimize it using Agent Platform Managed Training.

question:
Your organization manages an online message board. A few months ago, you discovered an increase in toxic language and bullying on the
 message board. You deployed an automated text classifier that flags certain comments as toxic or harmful. Now some users are reporting that
 benign comments referencing their religion are being misclassified as abusive. Upon further inspection, you find that your classifier's false
 positive rate is higher for comments that reference certain underrepresented religious groups. Your team has a limited budget and is already
 overextended. What should you do?
option_a: Add synthetic training data where those phrases are used in non-toxic ways.
option_b: Remove the model and replace it with human moderation.
option_c: Replace your model with a different text classifier.
option_d: Raise the threshold for comments to be considered toxic or harmful.
explanation: The problem is a subgroup-specific false-positive disparity caused by underrepresentation. Adding carefully reviewed non-toxic examples that use the affected phrases gives the model counterexamples and directly targets the failure mode. Raising the global threshold may reduce all detections and does not specifically remediate subgroup bias.

question:
You work for a magazine distributor and need to build a model that predicts which customers will renew their subscriptions for the upcoming year.
 Using your company’s historical data as your training set, you created a TensorFlow model and deployed it to Vertex AI. You need to determine
 which customer attribute has the most predictive power for each prediction served by the model. What should you do?
option_a:
Stream prediction results to BigQuery. Use BigQuery’s CORR(X1, X2) function to calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between each
 feature and the target variable.
option_b:
Use Vertex Explainable AI. Submit each prediction request with the explain' keyword to retrieve feature attributions using the sampled
 Shapley method.
option_c:
Use Agent Platform Workbench user-managed notebooks to perform a Lasso regression analysis on your model, which will eliminate features
 that do not provide a strong signal.
option_d:
Use the What-If tool in Google Cloud to determine how your model will perform when individual features are excluded. Rank the feature
 importance in order of those that caused the most significant performance drop when removed from the model.
explanation: Vertex Explainable AI returns feature attributions for each individual prediction. Sampled Shapley is suitable for tabular inputs and directly answers which customer attributes contributed most to each served result. Correlation and feature-ablation analyses are global and do not explain a single prediction.
terminology_notes: Generic or unrecognized Vertex AI reference requires contextual review.
exam_objectives: Identifying risks to AI solutions
topics: Explainability; Agents; BigQuery; Workbench

question:
You are an ML engineer at a manufacturing company. You are creating a classification model for a predictive maintenance use case. You need to
 predict whether a crucial machine will fail in the next three days so that the repair crew has enough time to fix the machine before it breaks.
 Regular maintenance of the machine is relatively inexpensive, but a failure would be very costly. You have trained several binary classifiers to
 predict whether the machine will fail, where a prediction of 1 means that the ML model predicts a failure.
 You are now evaluating each model on an evaluation dataset. You want to choose a model that prioritizes detection while ensuring that more than
 50% of the maintenance jobs triggered by your model address an imminent machine failure. Which model should you choose?
option_a: The model with the highest area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC ROC) and precision greater than 0.5
option_b: The model with the lowest root mean squared error (RMSE) and recall greater than 0.5.
option_c: The model with the highest recall where precision is greater than 0.5.
option_d: The model with the highest precision where recall is greater than 0.5.
explanation: A machine failure is much more costly than preventive maintenance, so false negatives must be minimized. Choose the model with the highest recall while enforcing an acceptable precision floor to limit excessive maintenance alerts.
exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions
topics: Evaluation Metrics; Classification; Model Monitoring

question:
You built a custom ML model using scikit-learn. Training time is taking longer than expected. You decide to migrate your model to Vertex AI
 Training, and you want to improve the model’s training time. What should you try out first?
option_a: Train your model in a distributed mode using multiple Compute Engine VMs.
option_b: Train your model using Agent Platform Managed Training with CPUs.
option_c: Migrate your model to TensorFlow, and train it using Agent Platform Managed Training.
option_d: Train your model using Agent Platform Managed Training with GPUs.
explanation: Most scikit-learn estimators are CPU-based and do not automatically use GPUs or distributed workers. The first managed migration step is therefore to run the existing code on appropriately sized Vertex AI CPU machines, then profile and optimize before considering a framework rewrite.

exam_objectives: Training models
topics: Custom Training; Training Hardware; Model Optimization; Agents

question:
You are an ML engineer at a retail company. You have built a model that predicts a coupon to offer an ecommerce customer at checkout based on
 the items in their cart. When a customer goes to checkout, your serving pipeline, which is hosted on Google Cloud, joins the customer's existing
 cart with a row in a BigQuery table that contains the customers' historic purchase behavior and uses that as the model's input. The web team is
 reporting that your model is returning predictions too slowly to load the coupon offer with the rest of the web page. How should you speed up your
 model's predictions?
option_a: Attach an NVIDIA P100 GPU to your deployed model’s instance.
option_b: Use a low latency database for the customers’ historic purchase behavior.
option_c: Deploy your model to more instances behind a load balancer to distribute traffic.
option_d: Create a materialized view in BigQuery with the necessary data for predictions.
explanation: BigQuery is optimized for analytics, not low-latency per-request feature lookup. Moving historical customer features to a low-latency online store removes the serving bottleneck. More model replicas or a GPU will not fix slow feature retrieval.
exam_objectives: Scaling online model serving; Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: Feature Store; Online Inference; BigQuery; Pipelines

question:
You work for a small company that has deployed an ML model with autoscaling on Vertex AI to serve online predictions in a production
 environment. The current model receives about 20 prediction requests per hour with an average response time of one second. You have retrained
 the same model on a new batch of data, and now you are canary testing it, sending ~10% of production traffic to the new model. During this
 canary test, you notice that prediction requests for your new model are taking between 30 and 180 seconds to complete. What should you do?
option_a: Submit a request to raise your project quota to ensure that multiple prediction services can run concurrently.
option_b: Turn off auto-scaling for the online prediction service of your new model. Use manual scaling with one node always available.
option_c:
Remove your new model from the production environment. Compare the new model and existing model codes to identify the cause of the
 performance bottleneck.
option_d:
Remove your new model from the production environment. For a short trial period, send all incoming prediction requests to BigQuery.
 Request batch predictions from your new model, and then use the Data Labeling Service to validate your model’s performance before
 promoting it to production.
explanation: At about two requests per hour to the canary model, autoscaling can scale to zero or incur cold-start delays. Keeping one replica always available removes cold starts and is appropriate for a low-traffic canary, although it increases baseline cost.
terminology_notes: Generic or unrecognized Vertex AI reference requires contextual review.
exam_objectives: Scaling online model serving
topics: Autoscaling; BigQuery; Batch Inference; Deployment Strategies

question:
You want to train an AutoML model to predict house prices by using a small public dataset stored in BigQuery. You need to prepare the data and
 want to use the simplest, most efficient approach. What should you do?
option_a:
Write a query that preprocesses the data by using BigQuery and creates a new table. Create a Agent Platform managed dataset with the new
 table as the data source.
option_b: Use Dataflow to preprocess the data. Write the output in TFRecord format to a Cloud Storage bucket.
option_c:
Write a query that preprocesses the data by using BigQuery. Export the query results as CSV files, and use those files to create a Vertex AI
 managed dataset.
option_d:
Use a Agent Platform Workbench notebook instance to preprocess the data by using the pandas library. Export the data as CSV files, and use
 those files to create a Agent Platform managed dataset.
explanation: For a small dataset already in BigQuery, preprocessing with SQL and creating a new BigQuery table is the simplest path. Vertex AI can import the resulting table directly, avoiding Dataflow, notebook, and CSV export overhead.

question:
You developed a Vertex AI ML pipeline that consists of preprocessing and training steps and each set of steps runs on a separate custom Docker
 image. Your organization uses GitHub and GitHub Actions as CI/CD to run unit and integration tests. You need to automate the model retraining
 workflow so that it can be initiated both manually and when a new version of the code is merged in the main branch. You want to minimize the
 steps required to build the workflow while also allowing for maximum flexibility. How should you configure the CI/CD workflow?
option_a:
Trigger a Cloud Build workflow to run tests, build custom Docker images, push the images to Artifact Registry, and launch the pipeline in
 Agent Platform Pipelines.
option_b:
Trigger GitHub Actions to run the tests, launch a job on Cloud Run to build custom Docker images, push the images to Artifact Registry, and
 launch the pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines.
option_c:
Trigger GitHub Actions to run the tests, build custom Docker images, push the images to Artifact Registry, and launch the pipeline in Vertex
 AI Pipelines.
option_d:
Trigger GitHub Actions to run the tests, launch a Cloud Build workflow to build custom Docker images, push the images to Artifact Registry,
 and launch the pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines.
explanation: GitHub Actions should remain the CI/CD entry point because it must support both manual runs and branch merges. Delegating image builds to Cloud Build avoids maintaining a Docker build environment in GitHub runners, pushes images to Artifact Registry, and then launches Agent Platform Pipelines. This provides flexibility with less build infrastructure management.

question:
You are working with a dataset that contains customer transactions. You need to build an ML model to predict customer purchase behavior. You
 plan to develop the model in BigQuery ML, and export it to Cloud Storage for online prediction. You notice that the input data contains a few
 categorical features, including product category and payment method. You want to deploy the model as quickly as possible. What should you do?
option_a:
Use the TRANSFORM clause with the ML.ONE_HOT_ENCODER function on the categorical features at model creation and select the
 categorical and non-categorical features.
option_b:
Use the ML.ONE_HOT_ENCODER function on the categorical features and select the encoded categorical features and non-categorical
 features as inputs to create your model.
option_c: Use the CREATE MODEL statement and select the categorical and non-categorical features.
option_d:
Use the ML.MULTI_HOT_ENCODER function on the categorical features, and select the encoded categorical features and non-categorical
 features as inputs to create your model.
explanation: Putting ML.ONE_HOT_ENCODER in the TRANSFORM clause stores the preprocessing with the BigQuery ML model. The same transformation is then applied consistently during prediction and is preserved when supported models are exported, reducing custom serving code.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: BigQuery ML; Feature Engineering; BigQuery; Cloud Storage

question:
You need to develop an image classification model by using a large dataset that contains labeled images in a Cloud Storage bucket. What should
 you do?
option_a:
Use Agent Platform Pipelines with the Kubeflow Pipelines SDK to create a pipeline that reads the images from Cloud Storage and trains the
 model.
option_b:
Use Agent Platform Pipelines with TensorFlow Extended (TFX) to create a pipeline that reads the images from Cloud Storage and trains the
 model.
option_c: Import the labeled images as a managed dataset in Vertex AI and use AutoML to train the model.
option_d: Convert the image dataset to a tabular format using Dataflow Load the data into BigQuery and use BigQuery ML to train the model.
explanation: Importing the labeled images into a Agent Platform managed dataset and using AutoML image classification is the fastest managed path. Building a custom Kubeflow or TFX pipeline is appropriate only when the AutoML workflow does not meet requirements.

question:
You are developing a model to detect fraudulent credit card transactions. You need to prioritize detection, because missing even one fraudulent
 transaction could severely impact the credit card holder. You used AutoML to tram a model on users' profile information and credit card
 transaction data After training the initial model, you notice that the model is failing to detect many fraudulent transactions. How should you adjust
 the training parameters in AutoML to improve model performance? (Choose two.)
option_a: Increase the score threshold
option_b: Decrease the score threshold.
option_c: Add more positive examples to the training set
option_d: Add more negative examples to the training set
option_e: Reduce the maximum number of node hours for training
explanation: Lowering the score threshold increases the number of transactions predicted as fraud and therefore raises recall, though it also increases false positives. Adding more positive fraud examples improves the model's ability to learn the rare class. More negative examples or less training time would not address missed fraud.
exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions
topics: Evaluation Metrics; Classification; AutoML; Model Monitoring

question:
You need to deploy a scikit-leam classification model to production. The model must be able to serve requests 24/7, and you expect millions of
 requests per second to the production application from 8 am to 7 pm. You need to minimize the cost of deployment. What should you do?
option_a: Deploy an online Vertex AI prediction endpoint. Set the max replica count to 1
option_b: Deploy an online Vertex AI prediction endpoint. Set the max replica count to 100
option_c: Deploy an online Vertex AI prediction endpoint with one GPU per replica. Set the max replica count to 1
option_d: Deploy an online Vertex AI prediction endpoint with one GPU per replica. Set the max replica count to 100
explanation: Millions of requests per second require horizontal autoscaling across many CPU replicas. A maximum of one replica cannot serve the peak, and GPUs are generally unnecessary for scikit-learn inference and would increase cost. The exact replica limit should be load-tested; 100 may still be insufficient.
terminology_notes: Prediction terminology may map to online or batch inference depending on context. | Generic or unrecognized Vertex AI reference requires contextual review.
exam_objectives: Scaling online model serving; Serving models
topics: Autoscaling; Online Inference; Training Hardware; Custom Training

question:
You work with a team of researchers to develop state-of-the-art algorithms for financial analysis. Your team develops and debugs complex models
 in TensorFlow. You want to maintain the ease of debugging while also reducing the model training time. How should you set up your training
 environment?
option_a: Configure a v3-8 TPU VM. SSH into the VM to train and debug the model.
option_b: Configure a v3-8 TPU node. Use Cloud Shell to SSH into the Host VM to train and debug the model.
option_c: Configure a n1 -standard-4 VM with 4 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. SSH into the VM and use ParameterServerStraregv to train the model.
option_d: Configure a n1-standard-4 VM with 4 NVIDIA P100 GPUs. SSH into the VM and use MultiWorkerMirroredStrategy to train the model.
explanation: A TPU VM provides direct SSH access to the TPU host and supports interactive TensorFlow development and debugging while accelerating training. TPU nodes use a separate host architecture and are less convenient for direct debugging. The model must use TPU-supported TensorFlow operations.
exam_objectives: Choosing appropriate hardware for training
topics: Training Hardware; Custom Training; Workbench; Troubleshooting

question:
You created an ML pipeline with multiple input parameters. You want to investigate the tradeoffs between different parameter combinations. The
 parameter options are
 • Input dataset
 • Max tree depth of the boosted tree regressor
 • Optimizer learning rate
 You need to compare the pipeline performance of the different parameter combinations measured in F1 score, time to train, and model
 complexity. You want your approach to be reproducible, and track all pipeline runs on the same platform. What should you do?
option_a:
1. Use BigQueryML to create a boosted tree regressor, and use the hyperparameter tuning capability.
 2. Configure the hyperparameter syntax to select different input datasets: max tree depths, and optimizer learning rates. Choose the grid
 search option.
option_b:
1. Create a Vertex AI pipeline with a custom model training job as part of the pipeline. Configure the pipeline’s parameters to include those
 you are investigating.
 2. In the custom training step, use the Bayesian optimization method with F1 score as the target to maximize.
option_c:
1. Create a Agent Platform Workbench notebook for each of the different input datasets.
 2. In each notebook, run different local training jobs with different combinations of the max tree depth and optimizer learning rate parameters.
 3. After each notebook finishes, append the results to a BigQuery table.
option_d:
1. Create an experiment in Experiments on Agent Platform.
 2. Create a Vertex AI pipeline with a custom model training job as part of the pipeline. Configure the pipeline’s parameters to include those you
 are investigating.
 3. Submit multiple runs to the same experiment, using different values for the parameters.
explanation: Experiments on Agent Platform tracks multiple pipeline runs, parameters, metrics, and artifacts on one platform. Submitting runs with different datasets and hyperparameters provides reproducible comparison of F1, training time, and model complexity rather than optimizing only a single target metric.

exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Tracking and running ML experiments

question:
You received a training-serving skew alert from a Agent Platform Model Monitoring job running in production. You retrained the model with more recent
 training data, and deployed it back to the Agent Platform endpoint, but you are still receiving the same alert. What should you do?
option_a: Update the model monitoring job to use a lower sampling rate.
option_b: Update the model monitoring job to use the more recent training data that was used to retrain the model.
option_c:
Temporarily disable the alert. Enable the alert again after a sufficient amount of new production traffic has passed through the Vertex AI
 endpoint.
option_d:
Temporarily disable the alert until the model can be retrained again on newer training data. Retrain the model again after a sufficient
 amount of new production traffic has passed through the Agent Platform endpoint.
explanation: The monitoring job is still comparing serving data with the old training baseline. After retraining, update or recreate the monitoring configuration so it uses the new training dataset; otherwise the same skew alert can persist even when the deployed model is current.
terminology_notes: Generic or unrecognized Vertex AI reference requires contextual review.
exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions; Automating model retraining
topics: Model Monitoring; Agents; Data Preparation; Online Inference

question:
You developed a custom model by using Vertex AI to forecast the sales of your company’s products based on historical transactional data. You
 anticipate changes in the feature distributions and the correlations between the features in the near future. You also expect to receive a large
 volume of prediction requests. You plan to use Agent Platform Model Monitoring for drift detection and you want to minimize the cost. What should you
 do?
option_a: Use the features for monitoring. Set a monitoring-frequency value that is higher than the default.
option_b: Use the features for monitoring. Set a prediction-sampling-rate value that is closer to 1 than 0.
option_c: Use the features and the feature attributions for monitoring. Set a monitoring-frequency value that is lower than the default.
option_d: Use the features and the feature attributions for monitoring. Set a prediction-sampling-rate value that is closer to 0 than 1.
explanation: Monitoring both input features and feature attributions helps detect changes in distributions and in relationships that influence predictions. With high request volume, sampling closer to zero controls monitoring cost while still providing a large absolute sample. The rate must remain high enough for reliable statistics.

exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions; Identifying risks to AI solutions
topics: Model Monitoring; Forecasting; Agents; Data Preparation

question:
You have recently trained a scikit-learn model that you plan to deploy on Vertex AI. This model will support both online and batch prediction. You
 need to preprocess input data for model inference. You want to package the model for deployment while minimizing additional code. What should
 you do?
option_a:
1. Upload your model to the Agent Platform Model Registry by using a prebuilt scikit-ieam prediction container.
 2. Deploy your model to Agent Platform Endpoints, and create a Agent Platform batch prediction job that uses the instanceConfig.instanceType setting to
 transform your input data.
option_b:
1. Wrap your model in a custom prediction routine (CPR). and build a container image from the CPR local model.
 2. Upload your scikit learn model container to Agent Platform Model Registry.
 3. Deploy your model to Agent Platform Endpoints, and create a Agent Platform batch prediction job
option_c:
1. Create a custom container for your scikit learn model.
 2. Define a custom serving function for your model.
 3. Upload your model and custom container to Agent Platform Model Registry.
 4. Deploy your model to Agent Platform Endpoints, and create a Agent Platform batch prediction job.
option_d:
1. Create a custom container for your scikit learn model.
 2. Upload your model and custom container to Agent Platform Model Registry.
 3. Deploy your model to Agent Platform Endpoints, and create a Agent Platform batch prediction job that uses the instanceConfig.instanceType setting to
 transform your input data.
explanation: A custom prediction routine lets preprocessing, model invocation, and postprocessing be packaged around a scikit-learn model with less serving boilerplate than writing a complete custom HTTP server. The same model package can support online and batch prediction on Vertex AI.

question:
You work for a food product company. Your company’s historical sales data is stored in BigQuery.You need to use Vertex AI’s custom training
 service to train multiple TensorFlow models that read the data from BigQuery and predict future sales. You plan to implement a data
 preprocessing algorithm that performs mm-max scaling and bucketing on a large number of features before you start experimenting with the
 models. You want to minimize preprocessing time, cost, and development effort. How should you configure this workflow?
option_a: Write the transformations into Spark that uses the spark-bigquery-connector, and use Dataproc to preprocess the data.
option_b: Write SQL queries to transform the data in-place in BigQuery.
option_c: Add the transformations as a preprocessing layer in the TensorFlow models.
option_d: Create a Dataflow pipeline that uses the BigQuerylO connector to ingest the data, process it, and write it back to BigQuery.
explanation: BigQuery SQL can perform min-max scaling and bucketing in place over large structured datasets using distributed execution. This avoids moving data through Dataproc or Dataflow and prevents repeating preprocessing inside every TensorFlow experiment.

question:
You have created a Vertex AI pipeline that includes two steps. The first step preprocesses 10 TB data completes in about 1 hour, and saves the
 result in a Cloud Storage bucket. The second step uses the processed data to train a model. You need to update the model’s code to allow you to
 test different algorithms. You want to reduce pipeline execution time and cost while also minimizing pipeline changes. What should you do?
option_a:
Add a pipeline parameter and an additional pipeline step. Depending on the parameter value, the pipeline step conducts or skips data
 preprocessing, and starts model training.
option_b: Create another pipeline without the preprocessing step, and hardcode the preprocessed Cloud Storage file location for model training.
option_c: Configure a machine with more CPU and RAM from the compute-optimized machine family for the data preprocessing step.
option_d: Enable caching for the pipeline job, and disable caching for the model training step.
explanation: Agent Platform Pipelines caching can reuse the successful preprocessing output when the component inputs, code, and configuration are unchanged. Disabling caching only for the model-training step ensures each algorithm experiment retrains while avoiding the one-hour, 10 TB preprocessing step.

question:
You work for a bank. You have created a custom model to predict whether a loan application should be flagged for human review. The input
 features are stored in a BigQuery table. The model is performing well, and you plan to deploy it to production. Due to compliance requirements the
 model must provide explanations for each prediction. You want to add this functionality to your model code with minimal effort and provide
 explanations that are as accurate as possible. What should you do?
option_a: Create an AutoML tabular model by using the BigQuery data with integrated Vertex Explainable AI.
option_b: Create a BigQuery ML deep neural network model and use the ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT method with the num_integral_steps parameter.
option_c:
Upload the custom model to Agent Platform Model Registry and configure feature-based attribution by using sampled Shapley with input

question:
You recently used XGBoost to train a model in Python that will be used for online serving. Your model prediction service will be called by a
 backend service implemented in Golang running on a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster. Your model requires pre and postprocessing steps.
 You need to implement the processing steps so that they run at serving time. You want to minimize code changes and infrastructure maintenance,
 and deploy your model into production as quickly as possible. What should you do?
option_a:
Use FastAPI to implement an HTTP server. Create a Docker image that runs your HTTP server, and deploy it on your organization’s GKE
 cluster.
option_b:
Use FastAPI to implement an HTTP server. Create a Docker image that runs your HTTP server, Upload the image to Agent Platform Model Registry
 and deploy it to a Agent Platform endpoint.
option_c:
Use the Predictor interface to implement a custom prediction routine. Build the custom container, upload the container to Vertex AI Model
 Registry and deploy it to a Agent Platform endpoint.
option_d:
Use the XGBoost prebuilt serving container when importing the trained model into Vertex AI. Deploy the model to a Agent Platform endpoint.
 Work with the backend engineers to implement the pre- and postprocessing steps in the Golang backend service.
explanation: A custom prediction routine packages Python pre- and postprocessing with the XGBoost predictor and deploys it to a managed Agent Platform endpoint. This minimizes changes to the Go backend and avoids operating a custom FastAPI service on GKE.

question:
You recently deployed a pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines that trains and pushes a model to a Agent Platform endpoint to serve real-time traffic. You need
 to continue experimenting and iterating on your pipeline to improve model performance. You plan to use Cloud Build for CI/CD You want to quickly
 and easily deploy new pipelines into production, and you want to minimize the chance that the new pipeline implementations will break in
 production. What should you do?
option_a:
Set up a CI/CD pipeline that builds and tests your source code. If the tests are successful, use the Google. Cloud console to upload the
 built container to Artifact Registry and upload the compiled pipeline to Agent Platform Pipelines.
option_b:
Set up a CI/CD pipeline that builds your source code and then deploys built artifacts into a pre-production environment. Run unit tests in the
 pre-production environment. If the tests are successful deploy the pipeline to production.
option_c:
Set up a CI/CD pipeline that builds and tests your source code and then deploys built artifacts into a pre-production environment. After a
 successful pipeline run in the pre-production environment, deploy the pipeline to production.
option_d:
Set up a CI/CD pipeline that builds and tests your source code and then deploys built artifacts into a pre-production environment. After a
 successful pipeline run in the pre-production environment, rebuild the source code and deploy the artifacts to production.
explanation: A safe CI/CD flow builds and tests the source, deploys the same built artifacts to a pre-production environment, runs the complete pipeline there, and promotes those artifacts to production only after a successful run. Rebuilding before production can introduce untested differences.

question:
You work for a bank with strict data governance requirements. You recently implemented a custom model to detect fraudulent transactions. You
 want your training code to download internal data by using an API endpoint hosted in your project’s network. You need the data to be accessed in
 the most secure way, while mitigating the risk of data exfiltration. What should you do?
option_a: Enable VPC Service Controls for peerings, and add Vertex AI to a service perimeter.
option_b:
Create a Cloud Run endpoint as a proxy to the data. Use Identity and Access Management (IAM) authentication to secure access to the
 endpoint from the training job.
option_c: Configure VPC Peering with Vertex AI, and specify the network of the training job.
option_d: Download the data to a Cloud Storage bucket before calling the training job.
explanation: VPC Service Controls adds a service perimeter around supported Google Cloud services and is specifically intended to reduce data-exfiltration risk. Private networking alone does not provide the same perimeter-based control. The training service and data services must both be configured within the supported perimeter design.

question:
You are deploying a new version of a model to a production Vertex Al endpoint that is serving traffic. You plan to direct all user traffic to the new
 model. You need to deploy the model with minimal disruption to your application. What should you do?
option_a:
1. Create a new endpoint
 2. Create a new model. Set it as the default version. Upload the model to Agent Platform Model Registry
 3. Deploy the new model to the new endpoint
 4. Update Cloud DNS to point to the new endpoint
option_b:
1. Create a new endpoint
 2. Create a new model. Set the parentModel parameter to the model ID of the currently deployed model and set it as the default version.
 Upload the model to Agent Platform Model Registry
 3. Deploy the new model to the new endpoint, and set the new model to 100% of the traffic.
option_c:
1. Create a new model. Set the parentModel parameter to the model ID of the currently deployed model. Upload the model to Vertex AI
 Model Registry.
 2. Deploy the new model to the existing endpoint, and set the new model to 100% of the traffic
option_d:
1. Create a new model. Set it as the default version. Upload the model to Agent Platform Model Registry
 2. Deploy the new model to the existing endpoint
explanation: Upload the new artifact as a version of the existing Model Registry model, deploy it to the existing endpoint, and shift the endpoint traffic split to 100% for the new deployment. This avoids changing the application's endpoint URL and minimizes disruption.

question:
You are training an ML model on a large dataset. You are using a TPU to accelerate the training process. You notice that the training process is
 taking longer than expected. You discover that the TPU is not reaching its full capacity. What should you do?
option_a: Increase the learning rate
option_b: Increase the number of epochs
option_c: Decrease the learning rate
option_d: Increase the batch size
explanation: A TPU that is underutilized often needs more work per step. Increasing the batch size can improve matrix-unit utilization and amortize input and synchronization overhead. The learning rate may then need retuning.

topics: Training Hardware; Model Optimization

question:
You work for a retail company. You have a managed tabular dataset in Vertex AI that contains sales data from three different stores. The dataset
 includes several features, such as store name and sale timestamp. You want to use the data to train a model that makes sales predictions for a
 new store that will open soon. You need to split the data between the training, validation, and test sets. What approach should you use to split the
 data?
option_a: Use Vertex AI manual split, using the store name feature to assign one store for each set
option_b: Use Vertex AI default data split
option_c: Use Vertex AI chronological split, and specify the sales timestamp feature as the time variable
option_d: Use Vertex AI random split, assigning 70% of the rows to the training set, 10% to the validation set, and 20% to the test set
explanation: Because the production target is an unseen store, evaluation should hold out entire stores rather than randomly or chronologically mixing rows from every store. A manual group split by store best measures generalization to a new store. With only three stores, the estimate will be noisy, so group cross-validation would be preferable outside the listed options.

question:
You have developed a BigQuery ML model that predicts customer chum, and deployed the model to Agent Platform Endpoints. You want to automate the
 retraining of your model by using minimal additional code when model feature values change. You also want to minimize the number of times that
 your model is retrained to reduce training costs. What should you do?
option_a:
1 Enable request-response logging on Agent Platform Endpoints
 2. Schedule a TensorFlow Data Validation job to monitor prediction drift
 3. Execute model retraining if there is significant distance between the distributions
option_b:

question:
You work for a telecommunications company. You’re building a model to predict which customers may fail to pay their next phone bill. The
 purpose of this model is to proactively offer at-risk customers assistance such as service discounts and bill deadline extensions. The data is
 stored in BigQuery and the predictive features that are available for model training include:
 - Customer_id
 - Age
 - Salary (measured in local currency)
 - Sex
 - Average bill value (measured in local currency)
 - Number of phone calls in the last month (integer)
 - Average duration of phone calls (measured in minutes)
 You need to investigate and mitigate potential bias against disadvantaged groups, while preserving model accuracy.
 What should you do?
option_a:
Determine whether there is a meaningful correlation between the sensitive features and the other features. Train a BigQuery ML boosted
 trees classification model and exclude the sensitive features and any meaningfully correlated features.
option_b:
Train a BigQuery ML boosted trees classification model with all features. Use the ML.GLOBAL_EXPLAIN method to calculate the global
 attribution values for each feature of the model. If the feature importance value for any of the sensitive features exceeds a threshold, discard
 the model and tram without this feature.
option_c:
Train a BigQuery ML boosted trees classification model with all features. Use the ML.EXPLAIN_PREDICT method to calculate the attribution
 values for each feature for each customer in a test set. If for any individual customer, the importance value for any feature exceeds a
 predefined threshold, discard the model and train the model again without this feature.
option_d:
Define a fairness metric that is represented by accuracy across the sensitive features. Train a BigQuery ML boosted trees classification
 model with all features. Use the trained model to make predictions on a test set. Join the data back with the sensitive features, and calculate
 a fairness metric to investigate whether it meets your requirements.
explanation: Fairness should be evaluated directly across protected-group slices using a metric tied to the use case. Train with all candidate features, score a held-out set, join predictions with sensitive attributes, and compare group metrics. Removing a sensitive field or any correlated proxy does not by itself guarantee fairness and can reduce accuracy.

question:
You are developing a model to detect fraudulent credit card transactions. You need to prioritize detection, because missing even one fraudulent
 transaction could severely impact the credit card holder. You used AutoML to train a model on users' profile information and credit card
 transaction data. After training the initial model, you notice that the model is failing to detect many fraudulent transactions. How should you
 increase the number of fraudulent transactions that are detected?
option_a: Add more non-fraudulent examples to the training set.
option_b: Reduce the maximum number of node hours for training.
option_c: Increase the probability threshold to classify a fraudulent transaction.
option_d: Decrease the probability threshold to classify a fraudulent transaction.
explanation: Lowering the classification threshold causes more transactions to be labeled as fraudulent, which raises recall and reduces false negatives. This is appropriate when missing fraud is especially costly, although it will usually increase false positives and should be tuned against the business cost.

question:
You work at an organization that maintains a cloud-based communication platform that integrates conventional chat, voice, and video
 conferencing into one platform. The audio recordings are stored in Cloud Storage. All recordings have a 16 kHz sample rate and are more than one
 minute long. You need to implement a new feature in the platform that will automatically transcribe voice call recordings into text for future
 applications, such as call summarization and sentiment analysis. How should you implement the voice call transcription feature while following
 Google-recommended practices?
option_a: Use the original audio sampling rate, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with synchronous recognition.
option_b: Use the original audio sampling rate, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with asynchronous recognition.
option_c: Downsample the audio recordings to 8 kHz, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with synchronous recognition.
option_d: Downsample the audio recordings to 8 kHz, and transcribe the audio by using the Speech-to-Text API with asynchronous recognition.
explanation: Recordings longer than one minute should use asynchronous, long-running Speech-to-Text recognition. Keep the original 16 kHz sample rate because downsampling discards acoustic information and provides no benefit.

Store the data in a Cloud Storage bucket, and create a custom container with your training application and its custom dependencies. In your

 (area under the ROC curve), has dropped significantly in production compared to its performance during training. How should you troubleshoot
 this problem?
option_a: Monitor the training/serving skew of feature values for requests sent to the endpoint.
option_b: Monitor the resource utilization of the endpoint, such as CPU and memory usage, to identify potential bottlenecks in performance.
option_c:
Enable Vertex Explainable AI feature attribution to analyze model predictions and understand the impact of each feature on the model's

option_d: Monitor the latency of the endpoint to determine whether predictions are being served within the expected time frame.
explanation: A large production AUC drop with the same deployed model commonly indicates that production feature values differ from the training distribution or that preprocessing differs between training and serving.  deployed it to a Agent Platform endpoint. The endpoint is currently using 1 e2-standard-2 machine with 2 vCPUs and 8 GB of memory. You discover that
 traffic on the gateway fluctuates to four times more than the endpoint's capacity. You need to address this issue by using the most cost-effective

 mimic famous authors if their style is detected. You have a large dataset of various authors' works, and you plan to host the model on a custom

question:
You deployed a conversational application that uses a large language model (LLM). The application has 1,000 users. You collect user feedback
 about the verbosity and accuracy of the model 's responses. The user feedback indicates that the responses are factually correct but users want
 different levels of verbosity depending on the type of question. You want the model to return responses that are more consistent with users'
 expectations, and you want to use a scalable solution. What should you do?
option_a:
Implement a keyword-based routing layer. If the user's input contains the words "detailed" or "description," return a verbose response. If the
 user's input contains the word "fact." re-prompt the language model to summarize the response and return a concise response.
option_b:
Ask users to provide examples of responses with the appropriate verbosity as a list of question and answer pairs. Use this dataset to
 perform supervised fine tuning of the foundational model. Re-evaluate the verbosity of responses with the tuned model.
option_c:
Ask users to indicate all scenarios where they expect concise responses versus verbose responses. Modify the application 's prompt to
 include these scenarios and their respective verbosity levels. Re-evaluate the verbosity of responses with updated prompts.
option_d:
Experiment with other proprietary and open-source LLMs. Perform A/B testing by setting each model as your application's default model.
 Choose a model based on the results.
explanation: The organization has user feedback that can be converted into examples pairing questions with appropriately concise or detailed responses. Supervised fine-tuning teaches the behavior more consistently and at greater scale than brittle keyword routing or continually expanding a long application prompt. A smaller prompt-only change should still be tested first when adequate.

question: Your organization’s marketing team wants to send biweekly scheduled emails to customers that are expected to spend above a variable threshold. This is the first ML use case for the marketing team, and you have been tasked with the implementation. After setting up a new Google Cloud project, you use Agent Platform Workbench to develop model training and batch inference with an XGBoost model on the transactional data stored in Cloud Storage. You want to automate the end-to-end pipeline that will securely provide the predictions to the marketing team, while minimizing cost and code maintenance. What should you do?
option_a: Create a scheduled pipeline on Agent Platform Pipelines that accesses the data from Cloud Storage, uses Agent Platform to perform training and batch prediction, and outputs a file in a Cloud Storage bucket that contains a list of all customer emails and expected spending.
option_b: Create a scheduled pipeline on Managed Service for Apache Airflow that accesses the data from Cloud Storage, copies the data to BigQuery, uses BigQuery ML to perform training and batch prediction, and outputs a table in BigQuery with customer emails and expected spending.
option_c: Create a scheduled notebook on Agent Platform Workbench that accesses the data from Cloud Storage, performs training and batch prediction on the managed notebook instance, and outputs a file in a Cloud Storage bucket that contains a list of all customer emails and expected spending.
option_d: Create a scheduled pipeline on Managed Service for Apache Airflow that accesses the data from Cloud Storage, uses Agent Platform to perform training and batch prediction, and sends an email to the marketing team’s Gmail group email with an attachment that contains an encrypted list of all customer emails and expected spending.
explanation: Official-guide answer: A. Agent Platform Pipelines and Cloud Storage are cost-effective and secure, and pipeline and schedule parameters can be updated in the Google Cloud console with minimal code interaction. question: You need to train an object detection model to identify bounding boxes around Post-it Notes® in an image. Post-it Notes can have a variety of background colors and shapes. option_a: Use Agent Platform TensorBoard to check whether the training metrics converge to typical values. Verify pipeline input configuration and steps have the expected values.
option_b: Upgrade to the latest version of the Agent Platform SDK and re-run the pipeline.
option_c: Determine the trained model’s location from the pipeline’s metadata in Agent Platform ML Metadata, and compare the trained model’s size to the previous model.
option_d: Request access to production systems. Get the training data’s location from the pipeline’s metadata in Agent Platform ML Metadata, and compare data volumes of the current run to the previous run.
explanation: Official-guide answer: A. TensorBoard provides a compact view of loss, accuracy, and other training metrics over time, allowing you to determine quickly whether training converged as expected; checking pipeline inputs and step configuration adds context. Upgrading the SDK does not validate model quality, model size is only a partial health signal, and requesting production-data access is slower and less secure.
exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions; Developing end-to-end ML pipelines
topics: Pipelines; Agents; AI Security; ML Metadata

question: You recently developed a custom ML model that was trained in Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform on a post-processed training dataset stored in BigQuery. You used a Cloud Run container to deploy the prediction service. The service performs feature lookup and pre-processing and sends a prediction request to an Agent Platform endpoint. You want to configure a comprehensive monitoring solution for training-serving skew that requires minimal maintenance. What should you do?
option_a: Create a Model Monitoring job for the endpoint that uses the training data in BigQuery to perform training-serving skew detection and uses email to send alerts. When an alert is received, use the console to diagnose the issue.
option_b: Update the model hosted in Agent Platform to enable request-response logging. Create a Data Studio dashboard that compares training data and logged data for potential training-serving skew and uses email to send a daily scheduled report.
option_c: Create a Model Monitoring job for the endpoint that uses the training data in BigQuery to perform training-serving skew detection and uses Cloud Logging to send alerts. Set up a Cloud Run function to initiate model retraining that is triggered when an alert is logged.
option_d: Update the model hosted in Agent Platform to enable request-response logging. Schedule a daily DataFlow Flex job that uses Tensorflow Data Validation to detect training-serving skew and uses Cloud Logging to send alerts. Set up a Cloud Run function to initiate model retraining that is triggered when an alert is logged.
explanation: Official-guide answer: A. Model Monitoring is the fully managed option for training-serving skew and therefore minimizes maintenance. Manual diagnosis is appropriate because skew can have several causes, including inconsistent preprocessing. Custom dashboards and Dataflow validation jobs add maintenance, and automatically retraining on every skew alert may not fix the underlying issue.
exam_objectives: Monitoring, testing, and troubleshooting AI solutions; Identifying risks to AI solutions
topics: Model Monitoring; BigQuery; Gemini; Agents

question: You recently used Agent Platform Inference to deploy a custom-trained model in production. The automated re-training pipeline made available a new model version that passed all unit and infrastructure tests. You want to define a rollout strategy for the new model version that guarantees an optimal user experience with zero downtime. What should you do?
option_a: Release the new model version in the same endpoint. Use traffic splitting in Agent Platform Inference to route a small random subset of requests to the new version and, if the new version is successful, gradually route the remaining traffic to it.
option_b: Release the new model version in a new endpoint. Update the application to send all requests to both endpoints, and log the predictions from the new endpoint. If the new version is successful, route all traffic to the new application.
option_c: Deploy the current model version with an Istio resource in Google Kubernetes Engine, and route production traffic to it. Deploy the new model version, and use Istio to route a small random subset of traffic to it. If the new version is successful, gradually route the remaining traffic to it.
option_d: Install Seldon Core and deploy an Istio resource in Google Kubernetes Engine. Deploy the current model version and the new model version using the multi-armed bandit algorithm in Seldon to dynamically route requests between the two versions before eventually routing all traffic over to the best-performing version.
explanation: Official-guide answer: B. A shadow deployment sends production requests to both versions while keeping the current model’s response user-facing, so the new model can be evaluated without affecting user experience and with zero downtime. Canary and multi-armed-bandit approaches expose some users to the new version and therefore cannot guarantee an unaffected experience.
exam_objectives: Serving models
topics: Deployment Strategies; Agents; GKE; Pipelines

question:
Your company manages an ecommerce website. You developed an ML model that recommends additional products to users in near real time based on items currently in the user’s cart. The workflow will include the following processes:

1. The website will send a Pub/Sub message with the relevant data, and then receive a message with the prediction from Pub/Sub.
2. Predictions will be stored in BigQuery.
3. The model will be stored in a Cloud Storage bucket and will be updated frequently.

You want to minimize prediction latency and the effort required to update the model. How should you reconfigure the architecture?
option_a: Write a Cloud Run function that loads the model into memory for prediction. Configure the function to be triggered when messages are sent to Pub/Sub.
option_b: Expose the model as an Agent Platform endpoint. Write a custom DoFn in a Dataflow job that calls the endpoint for prediction.
option_c: Use the RunInference API with WatchFilePattern in a Dataflow job that wraps around the model and serves predictions.
option_d: Create a pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines that performs preprocessing, prediction, and postprocessing. Configure the pipeline to be triggered by a Cloud Run function when messages are sent to Pub/Sub.
explanation: Official-guide answer: C. Dataflow RunInference with WatchFilePattern keeps inference local to the pipeline for low latency while allowing updated model files in Cloud Storage to be picked up seamlessly. Cloud Run functions can encounter request-rate and model-size limits, remote endpoint calls add latency, and Agent Platform Pipelines are not designed for low-latency per-message inference.
exam_objectives: Serving models; Developing end-to-end ML pipelines
topics: Dataflow; Model Optimization; Online Inference; Agents

question: A support application must summarize long customer case files and answer follow-up questions. Most requests reuse the same large case file, while the user question changes. You want to reduce repeated input processing cost and latency without changing model behavior. What should you do?
option_a: Store the case file in a context cache and reuse the cache for follow-up requests.
option_b: Fine-tune the model on every case file before answering questions.
option_c: Generate embeddings for the case file and always send every chunk to the model.
option_d: Increase the output token limit and lower the temperature.
explanation: Context caching is designed for repeated requests that share a large prefix or body of context. Reusing cached context can reduce processing cost and latency. Fine-tuning is not appropriate for transient per-case knowledge, and sending every chunk defeats the optimization.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models
topics: Context Caching; Gemini; Embeddings; Fine Tuning

question: A team is building a high-volume classification service with Gemini. The labels and output JSON schema are fixed, the task is simple, and latency and cost are more important than deep reasoning. Which approach is most appropriate?
option_a: Use the largest available reasoning model with maximum thinking budget.
option_b: Use a Flash-class Gemini model with constrained structured output.
option_c: Use a multimodal embedding model and nearest-neighbor search only.
option_d: Fine-tune an image generation model on the labels.
explanation: A Flash-class Gemini model is generally the best fit for high-throughput, latency-sensitive tasks, and structured output constrains responses to the required schema. A larger reasoning model would add unnecessary cost and latency.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models
topics: Gemini; Structured Output; Model Optimization; Embeddings

question: You are designing prompts for a production extraction application. You need predictable JSON and want to reduce accidental instruction conflicts. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)
option_a: Define the required response schema using structured output.
option_b: Place untrusted document text inside the system instruction.
option_c: Separate system-level rules from user-provided content.
option_d: Use the highest temperature available.
option_e: Ask the model to explain its hidden reasoning before returning JSON.
explanation: Structured output enforces the expected schema, and separating trusted system instructions from untrusted user content reduces instruction ambiguity and prompt-injection risk. Untrusted text should not be promoted into system instructions, and high temperature reduces predictability.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models; Identifying risks to AI solutions
topics: Structured Output; Prompt Engineering; Foundation Models

question: A legal research assistant must answer questions using current public court information and provide source grounding. The underlying information changes frequently and should not be embedded permanently in model weights. What should you do?
option_a: Use supervised fine-tuning with weekly court documents.
option_b: Increase the model temperature so it explores more possibilities.
option_c: Use grounding with Google Search or an approved search data source at inference time.
option_d: Use prompt examples that contain old court cases.
explanation: Grounding retrieves current information at inference time and can provide source attribution. Fine-tuning changes behavior and patterns but is not the right mechanism for rapidly changing factual knowledge.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models; Identifying risks to AI solutions
topics: Grounding; Prompt Engineering; Fine Tuning; Foundation Models

question: A Gemini application produces correct answers but often adds prose before and after the required object, causing downstream parsing failures. You want the lowest-maintenance fix. What should you do?
option_a: Parse the prose with a custom regular expression and maintain it as outputs change.
option_b: Fine-tune the model solely to remove introductory sentences.
option_c: Switch to batch prediction.
option_d: Use response schema or structured output to require the object format.
explanation: Structured output is the managed, low-maintenance way to constrain generated responses to a schema. Regex parsing remains brittle, and fine-tuning is excessive for a formatting constraint.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models
topics: Structured Output; Gemini; Fine Tuning; Batch Inference

question: An application sends a 500-page policy manual with every request. Only a few sections are relevant to each question, and questions rarely repeat. You want to reduce token usage while keeping answers grounded in the manual. What should you do?
option_a: Chunk and embed the manual, retrieve the most relevant passages, and send only those passages to Gemini.
option_b: Use context caching for the entire manual indefinitely.
option_c: Supervised-fine-tune Gemini on the manual and delete the source documents.
option_d: Increase the maximum context window and always include all pages.
explanation: RAG is appropriate when only a small subset of a large corpus is relevant per request. Context caching is strongest when the same large context is reused frequently; fine-tuning is not a substitute for factual retrieval.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models; Building models given the task considering cost, complexity, latency, and scalability
topics: RAG; Model Optimization; Gemini; Context Caching

question: A RAG system retrieves semantically related documents, but many are irrelevant because they discuss the same broad topic. The corpus includes reliable product, region, and effective-date metadata. What is the best first improvement?
option_a: Increase generation temperature.
option_b: Apply metadata filters during retrieval in addition to vector similarity.
option_c: Fine-tune the generative model on all retrieved documents.
option_d: Return more chunks regardless of relevance.
explanation: Metadata filtering narrows the candidate set using known constraints and complements semantic similarity. Increasing temperature or returning more chunks does not improve retrieval precision.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models; Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: RAG; Vector Search; Evaluation Metrics; Foundation Models

question: You changed the embedding model used for new documents in a vector index, but old vectors were created with a different model and dimensionality. Retrieval quality immediately degraded. What should you do?
option_a: Keep both vector types in the same index and compare raw dot products.
option_b: Increase the LLM temperature.
option_c: Re-embed the corpus with one compatible embedding model and rebuild or migrate the index.
option_d: Tune only the generation model.
explanation: Query and document embeddings must be produced in a compatible vector space and dimensionality. Mixing embeddings from incompatible models makes similarity scores meaningless, so the corpus should be re-embedded and the index rebuilt or migrated.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models; Exploring and preprocessing data for ML
topics: Embeddings; Vector Search; Foundation Models

question: You are evaluating a RAG pipeline separately from the final answer generator. Which two measurements most directly assess retrieval quality? (Choose two.)
option_a: GPU utilization of the generation endpoint.
option_b: Recall of relevant documents in the retrieved set.
option_c: BLEU score of the final answer only.
option_d: Precision or relevance of retrieved chunks.
option_e: Number of output tokens generated.
explanation: Retrieval quality is directly measured by whether relevant documents are found (recall) and how many retrieved items are relevant (precision/relevance). Endpoint utilization and output length are operational metrics, not retrieval-quality metrics.
exam_section: Collaborating within and across teams to manage data and models
exam_objectives: Tracking and running ML experiments; Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models
topics: RAG; Evaluation Metrics; Pipelines; Training Hardware

question: A company already has an enterprise search data store with access controls, document ingestion, and ranking. It wants to ground Gemini answers in that corpus with minimal new infrastructure. What should it use?
option_a: A custom TPU training job.
option_b: Cloud SQL full table scans for every prompt.
option_c: A supervised tuning job that memorizes all documents.
option_d: Vertex AI Search as the grounding or retrieval data source.
explanation: Vertex AI Search can provide a managed retrieval backend and grounding source while reusing existing ingestion, ranking, and access-control capabilities. Custom training or full scans add unnecessary complexity.
terminology_notes: Search products have multiple new names depending on use case. | Generic or unrecognized Vertex AI reference requires contextual review.
exam_objectives: Building AI solutions using Google Cloud AI APIs or foundational models; Identifying risks to AI solutions
